title: Lane A ships the answers next to the problems, which is the pilot's worst defect repeating
description:
Lane A delivers "statement + frozen reference + commented reference" as one bundle. Nothing says
WHERE Frank receives any of it, and no bead covers delivery.

**This is the pilot's worst defect, repeating.** The answer key sat in the critic-readable
directory carrying the words "Never show this to a critic", built by the same session that had
quoted §6b.1 two hours earlier. §6b.1: "Telling an agent not to look at the answers does not work.
Isolation must be structural." §2.4 says the `tla-practice`/`tla-answers` split "is a leak defense,
not a preference, so it does not get simplified into two directories of this repo later."

And it is v1's format failure. The post-mortem's J04 finding: "six items with the answers printed
in the next paragraph." §7.4 records the ENSEEIHT counter-technique, withhold practice solutions,
which the plan ignores.

Frank gets ONE first contact per problem, ever. With the reference and commentary a `ls` away, in a
repo he owns and debugs in, the first impasse becomes a peek. §9.9's "read the commentary after
attempting" then has no enforcement but willpower, which is exactly what §6b.1 rejects. Batch-1
telemetry, which is the entire reason §7.0 batches, is contaminated at the source.

**Fix, and it needs no Stage 4 machinery.** A statements-only delivery point outside this repo (or
`tla-practice/` scaffolded as a bare directory), with reference and commentary released per problem
only after an attempt is recorded. Two directories and one rule.

**Blocks shipping any problem to Frank.**

Files: (delivery scaffold, path TBD)
close_reason:
Delivery boundary built at /home/frank/tla-practice/ — problems in problems/, attempts in attempts/, references released to released/ only after an attempt is logged. Rationale and the §6b.1 / §2.4 / v1-J04 lineage are captured in drawer_tla_puzzles_decisions_89795ff4c47c0358e2ea81e9 (revised plan, CORRECTION 1) and drawer_tla_puzzles_milestones_2663e752389e002d8e85ceb5.

Deliberately outside the repo: the repo is the answers side (pilot/, authoring/) and a learner working inside it would have the reference an ls away, which is the instruction-isolation §6b.1 rejects. No Stage 4 machinery required, two directories and one rule.

The pilot problem is staged there as a warm-up with honest framing. The attempt log carries §6b.4's load-bearing question — were the rules unclear or was the modeling unclear — which is the only field that distinguishes a broken problem from a hard one and which nobody can infer from outside the learner's head.

Enforcement of 'nothing releases until an attempt is logged' is procedural, not mechanical. Worth a follow-up if it slips.

title: RESUME: read bd ready and the revised plan drawer
description:
Resume point after the 2026-08-07 wave. **This bead is a pointer, not a document.** The work lives
where loom keeps work: in beads, in drawers, and in the repo.

## Where to actually look

1. **`bd ready`** — the next-session brief, in dependency order. It is authoritative. The ordering
   is encoded as dependency edges rather than written as a list, so a blocked item will not surface
   until its blocker closes.
2. **`drawer_tla_puzzles_decisions_89795ff4c47c0358e2ea81e9`** — the operative plan, REVISED after
   two red-team passes. Read this before planning anything.
3. **`drawer_tla_puzzles_milestones_2663e752389e002d8e85ceb5`** — what happened and why.
4. **`V2-PLAN.md` §6** — rewritten 2026-08-07. The pipeline you run is the new one. Anyone working
   from memory of §6 is working from a document that no longer exists.
5. **`bd memories`** — three central-facing hazards recorded from this wave.

## The one-line plan

Frank's first attempt gates the rest of the batch. Author ONE problem properly, deliver it through
`/home/frank/tla-practice/`, and let what he reports shape problems 2-6.

## Model assignment, from evidence rather than preference

Central on **Fable**: its two red-teams and the §6 rewrite were the highest-leverage work of the
wave, all judgment-over-prose, and it is the abundant budget pool. Treat it as a trial — nobody has
seen Fable as central, only as a subagent.

Technical lanes on **Opus**: its wins were all deep measurement (the refinement.sh guard bypass, the
nine-shape exit-code derivation, the grade.sh cluster).

**Send `tla-krw5` to Opus specifically.** Fable wrote all three descriptions, and a same-family
review is the correlated blind spot the mixed-panel result exists to break.

## The irreversible item

`tla-kl5.17`, the holdout. Raised to P0. The honest window closes the moment batch 1 reaches Frank,
because after that every authored problem comes from a pipeline being tuned around him. Everything
else on the queue can be redone later. This cannot.

## Archive

`/home/frank/tla-puzzles-handoff/` holds a prose handoff written before this bead existed, plus
rescued scratchpad artifacts. **It is an archive, not the source of truth** — the descriptions it
carried are now committed under `authoring/`. Prefer bd and the drawers.

title: Stage 5 §7.2 — build the ~5-problem holdout set early and never tune it
description:
Goal: build ~5 problems EARLY, NEVER tune them, and reserve them for a DELAYED TRANSFER CHECK on
a different system. This is the only honest measurement the research endorses — performance
during practice is an unreliable index of learning, which is the same finding that killed v1.

Build them early precisely so they CANNOT be shaped by telemetry later. A holdout built after the
batches would be contaminated by everything learned from them, which is the whole failure mode.

DO NOT SITE THE HOLDOUT IN S7 OR S8 (§2.2 caveat 3). Migration and UI flows are inherently
software-shaped and Frank knows software — the mitigation is that the SITUATION is still novel to
him, but those problems are weaker instruments for measuring modeling ability and a holdout is
exactly where instrument quality matters most.

Files: (tla-answers/ — outside this repo)
acceptance_criteria: 5 problems built and sealed; sited outside S7/S8; a written rule recorded that they are never revised.
notes:
TIME-CRITICAL as of 2026-08-07, and currently unowned by the operative plan.

The research audit sharpened why 'early' is load-bearing: §7.0 makes all post-batch-1 authoring downstream of Frank's telemetry, and §7.1 names him as simultaneously subject and instrument. So the honest window for building an untuned holdout closes the moment batch 1 reaches him. After that, every authored problem comes from a pipeline being tuned around him, and a holdout built then is no longer the untuned instrument §7.2 describes.

Concretely: author 2-3 extra problems in the same wave as the first delivery, seed them from the reserve domains (blood bank, clinical trial cohorts), avoid S7/S8 per §2.2 caveat 2, freeze them, and stop touching them. Marginal cost is a few agent invocations against a budget §7.0 calls the intended scale at ~480.

Note that §7.2 calls delayed transfer on an untuned holdout 'the only honest measurement the research endorses', and it is presently the only measurement in the project with no owner.

title: Exercise set: learntla core ch.5
description:
Goal: 3-5 drills for learntla core ch.5, 10-15 minutes each, mixed formats (write-from-prompt, complete-the-skeleton, predict-then-check). Together they cover most of the chapter's major themes per the sheet.

Files: exercises/ch05/EXERCISES.md, exercises/ch05/starters/, exercises/ch05/references/, exercises/ch05/COVERAGE.md, exercises/ch05/reports/

Rules: constructs from ch.2-5 only, cited against the sheets. Surface content differs from the chapter's running examples. Expected outcomes are representation-robust, never state counts. Default shape is a pass run plus a fail run per exercise. Predict-then-check exercises commit the prediction to LOG.md before running TLC.

title: Adversarially review the three system descriptions before any reference author runs
description:
Three system descriptions are drafted in `authoring/{museum,custody,seedlib}/DESCRIPTION.md` and
none has been reviewed. **No reference author dispatches against an unreviewed description.**

This gate exists because central wrote a malformed observation operator TWICE on the pilot and
caught neither. First as `[issued |-> BOOLEAN, ...]`, which in TLA+ is a constant record whose
fields are sets: it does not depend on state and cannot be a grading interface. Then as an operator
that under-exposed, carrying no amendment count, so a whole rule of the system was invisible at the
graded interface and ungradable in principle. Both were found by workers, four and eight dispatches
downstream.

**Dispatch to Opus, not Fable.** All three descriptions were written by Fable, and the mixed-panel
result says depth of justification diverges across model families even where content does not. A
same-family review is the correlated blind spot the panel exists to break.

What the reviewer checks, per description:

- Every `Observe` field is **state-dependent**. Not a type, not a set.
- **Sufficiency**: walk every rule. A rule invisible through the operator is ungradable in
  principle, and either the operator gains a field or the rule goes. This is the pilot's second
  failure and it is not obvious from reading.
- **Representation-neutrality**: a field named after a variable, or one that forces a side of a
  declared fork, is a defect. Each description names its forks; check none is closed by the
  operator.
- **§3.2**: fixes the SYSTEM, leaves the REPRESENTATION open.
- **§2.2 caveat 2**: genuinely self-contained. All three domains are deliberately unfamiliar, so
  Frank cannot repair an ambiguity from experience.
- **The declared ambiguities**: each description lists nine or ten it resolved with the alternative
  it rejected. Audit the choices; do not accept the list because it is candid.

Deliver a per-description verdict: fit to author against, or send back with the specific defect.

The review also named the third Observe-family failure shape (a field exists, no property constrains the rule) and found it in all three. Full report preserved in drawer_tla_puzzles_findings_0f6739db4469fc3f07ff617b. Repairs spawned as tla-o8sc, which now blocks tla-jjo7.

title: seeded-bugs.sh's fragment validator is still line-anchored, the fourth site of one class
description:
`harness/seeded-bugs.sh:471` matches directives with `^[[:space:]]*(SPECIFICATION|...)` over text
stripped only of `\*` comments. **That is line-anchored, which is the exact hole `tla-nesz` closed
in `refinement.sh`.**

TLC's `.cfg` parser is token-oriented. Measured by the grade.sh worker, replicating
seeded-bugs.sh's own pipeline against `(* pad *) INVARIANT Bad`: **0 matches**. The token-oriented
pattern: **1 match**. So the validator added in `tla-40y` is defeatable the same way, and a
directive smuggled behind a block comment reaches TLC.

**This is the FOURTH site of one class**, and the sequence is worth recording because it shows how
the class propagated:

1. `refinement.sh` — line-anchored, defeated, hardened in `tla-nesz`. The same route also defeated
   the SYMMETRY refusal, where a false pass is silent and unrecoverable.
2. `seeded-bugs.sh` — validator added in `tla-40y`, believed sound, **still line-anchored**.
3. `grade.sh` — was unvalidated; `tla-j8yd` added a token-oriented validator.
4. This bead.

The grade.sh worker was briefed to "reuse `seeded-bugs.sh`'s validator rather than writing a third
one". Had it done so verbatim it would have imported the hole. It checked instead, found the
defect, and wrote the hardened form. **That brief was central's, and it was wrong.**

**The real fix is not a fourth copy.** Three files now carry three versions of one check and there
is no shared library, so "reuse" cannot happen inside any single file's footprint. Either extract a
sourced helper, or accept the duplication and gate it — a test asserting all three refuse
`(* pad *) INVARIANT Bad` would have caught this the day `tla-40y` landed.

title: The spread rule cannot tell richness from ambiguity, and refinement.sh already can
description:
Column A's success criterion is "all three succeed with genuinely different state representations →
target achieved." **An AMBIGUOUS statement produces the same signal.** Solvers resolve the ambiguity
differently, model different systems, and submit divergent specs — scored as target achieved.

§2.2 caveat 2 knows difficulty migrates invisibly on the all-FAIL side. Nothing controls the
all-SUCCEED side, where a §3.2 violation (the system was not actually fixed) reads as success.

**The fix costs one pipeline line and the tool is already built.** Check the panel's submissions
against EACH OTHER for behavioural equivalence over `Observe` — mutual refinement under the
observation, which `harness/refinement.sh` already performs for learner-against-reference.

- Same behaviour over `Observe`, different underlying representations → real modeling choice, the
  §2.1 target, confirmed rather than assumed.
- Divergent behaviour over `Observe` → the statement failed §3.2, and the spread was ambiguity
  wearing richness as a disguise.

That converts the spread rule's blind spot into a mechanical §3.2 gate.

Found by the research audit. Marked INFERRED there as an absence claim: no document it read — §6,
§9.7, §9.8, the pilot reports — proposes cross-checking panel members against each other. Critic E2
did the two-spec trick against its own work only.

title: Batch 1 has no telemetry channel, which is the entire reason §7.0 batches

of 0."

`tla-kl5.15` (attempt and impasse logging). "Reassess in the field" has no instrument.

Three things collide:

- §2.2 caveat 2 says the tutor log MUST distinguish a domain impasse from a modeling impasse, and
  that this is "load-bearing for §7.1. Without the distinction the refinement policy cannot be
  applied." Without it, an all-fail round reads as "underspecified" and you rewrite a statement
  that was fine.
- §7.1's only remaining channel is Frank's impressions, and §7.1 itself disqualifies them: 78% of

- §6b.4 calls first-contact attempts the research artifact no field has. One learner, one first

title: 4-6 all-column-A is blocked practice, an unadmitted §3.4 violation
description:
The build-out ships 4-6 problems that are ALL task shape A. §3.4 says "Interleave by idiom. Never
consecutive problems of one kind", d=0.83, preregistered cluster RCT, mechanism: "interleaved
practice requires students to choose a strategy and not merely execute a strategy."

§2.1 operationalized §3.4 into a checkable rule — walk the diagonal, "never get two consecutive
problems sharing either a situation or a task shape." §7.0 made the diagonal batch 1. The build-out
drops the diagonal and the invariant went with it silently.

**Two independent red-teams found this, and both noted the accounting failure rather than just the
violation.** The drawer scrupulously records its departure from §7.0 and its §3.7 cost, and never
mentions §3.4. Central proposed all-column-A and did not check it against a settled invariant three
sections above the one it did check.

**Worse: the three selected domains cluster on one idiom.** Museum is time, accrual and custody
over a published season calendar. Seed library is lending with return obligations over seasons.
Custody is a day-driven planning window. Two of three are bounded-lending-with-time-driven-
obligation, and all three are calendar-advanced. That approaches blocking on BOTH axes, which §3b
explicitly rejects as the coarsest grain.

**Fix: 4-6 CELLS, not 4-6 column-A.** Three or four A plus one B and one D along the diagonal. B and
D are cheaper to author than A, and the pilot proved the C path end to end so the machinery exists.
At minimum, enforce distinct situations and distinct mechanism families inside the A set, and order
them so no two calendar-idiom problems are adjacent.

Honest caveat from the audit: d=0.83 is school mathematics, and extending "never" to n=1 adult over
4-6 formal-methods problems is a directional bet rather than a measured effect. The bet is
reasonable. The absolutism is the plan's, not the study's.

title: The screen measures memorization, but abstraction-forcing is what binds
description:
A three-model recall probe over ten candidate domains (Opus, Fable, Sonnet, memory only, no tools)
returned **LOW memorization risk on 10 of 10**. The same probe's state sketches show convergence
ranging from LOW to HIGH.

**So memorization is not the binding constraint on this domain list. Abstraction-forcing is.**

§5.7 exists to stop a blind solver reproducing a memorized answer. Real, and the pilot confirmed
recognition happens — 6/6 named two-phase commit. But recognition did not collapse the hard half
of that problem, and across ten fresh domains nothing rates above LOW. Meanwhile §2.1's actual
target for column A is that a problem "admits real modeling choice", and the probe separates the
ten cleanly on exactly that.

**Opus produced the dual rating unprompted** — memorization AND convergence, scored separately —
which is the instrument fix Fable independently argued for. Fable's version: convergence on a data
shape is uninformative because ABO compatibility is world knowledge and every model encodes it the
same way; convergence on the POLICY choice is the signal, because that is where judgment lives.

Worked examples of the distinction, from the probes:

- **ski pass**: LOW memorization, HIGH convergence. "The system is a pure function of (pass, date)
  with a date variable bolted on... no concurrency and almost no invariant that can be violated by
  interleaving." Nobody published it and it is still a bad column-A problem.
- **escape room**: MEDIUM memorization from a source no corpus grep can see — "the hold/TTL/confirm
  reservation pattern is enormously represented in tutorial and blog material, so output here is
  likely to be stereotyped rather than reasoned."
- **library holds**: MEDIUM, and only one probe found why — the historic Library Problem
  (Kemmerer 1985, Wing's 1988 comparative study of twelve specifications). The problem is a
  published benchmark even though no TLA+ spec is in the corpus.
- **blood bank**: convergence on the compatibility matrix is forced and meaningless; convergence on
  the issue policy (FIFO-by-expiry vs nondeterministic) would be the real signal. One probe adds
  that the relation is asymmetric and inverts for plasma, "which resists boilerplate".

**Ask.** The screening protocol being built under `tla-7sp3` should score BOTH axes and report them
separately, and a column-A candidate should be rejected on high convergence even at LOW
memorization. A domain nobody has specified, that admits one obvious model, is a bad problem — and
today's screen would pass it without comment.

title: §6's spread rule reads the answer, but the spread is in the argument
description:
§6's spread rule reads the ANSWERS three blind solvers give. The mixed-panel re-run of the Stage 3
pilot (`pilot/reports/step6-mixed-panel.md`) shows that is the wrong place to look for a column-C
problem, and probably for others.

Six critics across three model families returned the same conjunct content, by the same route, in
one attempt each. Zero spread in the answer.

But five of the six PROVED their negative claim about the second gap, each with a different
constructed instrument — refinement under a mapping with a negative control, a projected
state-graph diff against a second correct spec, a stuttering simulation with exhaustive
enumeration, a trace-inclusion disjunction. The sixth reported "reasonably confident it can't be
done" after one candidate encoding, and flagged the weakness in its own rigor unprompted.

Same conclusion, materially different depth. That IS the spread, and the rule cannot see it,
because it looks at what was concluded rather than at what was built to conclude it.

This is the measurable form of `tla-y8tb`. That bead says column C's difficulty cannot live in
locating the gap and should move to arguing expressibility. This one says the GRADE should read the
argument, not the verdict — a critic who asserts inexpressibility and one who proves it have not
done the same work, and today they score identically.

Concretely, for the pilot's answer key: split gap-2 credit into (a) named the gap and (b) argued it
cannot be written over the observation operator, with (b) requiring a constructed check rather than
a claim. Five of six earn (b); one does not. The leakage pass proposed exactly this split
independently at step 5, before any critic ran.

title: §5.7 should return candidates and let a structural read give the verdict
description:
`tla-03d2`'s research recommends §5.7 stop returning verdicts and start returning candidates, with
the verdict coming from a structural read. Four steps, and the costs are measured rather than
estimated.

**S1 retrieval.** `screen.sh --offline`, with the two defects in the sibling bead fixed. Emits a
CANDIDATE list of corpus specs and exits 1. Never a verdict. About 0 s, offline.

**S2 recall probe.** Three parallel agents given ONLY the domain phrase — no spec, no statement,
no repo — asked to answer from memory with no tool calls: name the standard problem this reduces
to; name any published TLA+ spec of it with a `specifications/<dir>` path, do not guess; sketch
the VARIABLES and action names; then rate HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW that a competent LLM asked to spec this
would produce something structurally identical to an existing published spec.

**Built and run already.** 3 agents, 24 to 30 s each, fully parallel, 0 tool calls. Across the
three unscreened domains: 9/9 "no canonical named problem", 9/9 declined to guess a path, 9/9 LOW.

This measures model retrieval, which is what the survey drawer says §5.7 cares about, rather than
corpus contents. Its positives are checkable — a named path is verified with `test -d`. And it
cannot ratchet, because there is no vocabulary table to widen.

**Bonus that pays for itself.** All three probes returned near-identical VARIABLES for
apprenticeship hour logging. Three blind models converging on one state shape, while agreeing no
published spec exists, means there is no abstraction choice to make — which is a §5.7b question
answered by a §5.7 dispatch.

**S3 structural read.** One agent, only on S1 or S2 hits, about 10 minutes PER SPEC rather than per
domain. On the current 17 the candidate set collapses to roughly six distinct specs, because
domains share candidates, and the reads are reusable across batches.

**S4 verdict.** BURNED only if the structural read says the state shape, the enabling conditions
AND the hard property all carry.

**The anti-ratchet rule, which answers the concern on the parent bead.** The retrieval table is
keyed by CORPUS PATH, never by domain phrase. It may gain `specifications/byihive`; it may never
gain the word "ski pass". Domain-word entries grow with the space of English. Corpus entries grow
with a corpus of 111 directories that gains a few a year.

Honest limit carried from the research: the four-question allocator signature was derived from
reading four specs out of 111. It discriminates against the allocator and says nothing about the
other 110, so a domain that falls out of the allocator burn is un-assessed, not clear.

title: screen.sh burns on a prose match in a table the corpus warns about
description:
The §5.7 research (bead `tla-03d2`) found that most of the burn comes from `allocation`, and that
most of the `allocation` burn is a false positive. Two structural defects in `screen.sh` cause it,
and both are cheap.

**1. The README grep reads the second table's free-text column.** `allocat` matches two rows.
`examples-README.md:71` is a real name match, `Resource Allocator (specifications/allocator)`. The
other, `:131`, matches the word "allocation" inside the `Details` prose of `losa_ap` — in the
README's SECOND table, which the README itself introduces at `:115` with a warning that its
entries may be wrong or gone. And they are gone: `ls Examples/specifications/losa_ap` returns a
`README.md` and nothing else, and it is not one of the four submodules. **The spec files are not
in the corpus.**

So one of the two rows burning nine domains is a prose match in an uncurated table pointing at a
spec that is not there.

Fix: restrict the grep to the link text of column 1. Gate it — the fixture is that `allocat`
matches `:71` and not `:131`.

**2. One README row outranks three code-search hits.** `screen.sh:383-392` sets BURNED on any
non-empty rows. `screen.sh:411-416` requires more than `BURNED_AT` (4+) for the code-search
channel. A single markdown row is treated as stronger evidence than three real hits in real
repositories.

Fix: either bring the README channel to the same threshold, or state in the output why it differs.

Two more false positives, unrelated to `allocation`, both from the same one-row-is-proof rule:

- `queue` matches exactly one row, `Blocking Queue`. Its spec is a bounded buffer of
  undifferentiated messages whose interesting property is deadlock-freedom of Java's wait/notify.
  A library hold queue has identified patrons, positions, reneging and an expiring offer. The
  burn is the string "Queue".
- `two-phase` matches `:58 Two-Phase Handshaking`, which is an alternating-bit handshake with
  `VARIABLE v, x`, not two-phase commit. Municipal permit review still burns correctly, via the
  `transaction_commit` and `acp`/`nbacc`/`nbacg` rows.

**The tool corroborates the hand table where they overlap and is stricter everywhere else.** §2.2
suspected library holds, community garden and airline standby of being Resource Allocator in
different dress, and the screen agrees on all three. It then burns six more the table never
flagged.

Two things follow.

**Stage 5 cannot plan against this list.** §2.1 allocates 60 problems over 17 domains at roughly
3-4 each. Seven usable domains at best, three of them unverified, does not support that.

**Whether `allocation` is too coarse is a real question and I do not want it answered by
assumption.** It carries eight of the ten burns off two README rows. Almost any business domain
gives a limited thing to a requester. But `Resource Allocator` genuinely is that spec, and §5.7's
whole point is that name novelty is not mechanism novelty, so the strict reading may simply be
correct and the domain list simply wrong. Deciding that needs a look at whether a burned mechanism
under a §5.7b-rescued framing (agents and fallibility) is still burned, which §5.7b implies it may
not be.

Do NOT fix this by widening the synonym table until that question is settled. A table that
recognizes more phrasings burns MORE domains, not fewer.

title: Column C's difficulty cannot live in locating the gap
description:
Step 6 of the pilot ran three blind critics. All three found both seeded gaps. All three
submitted a byte-identical conjunct. All three took the same route, and it took seconds.

The route was not the one the leakage pass predicted. It was simpler: read Rule 3, read line 99,
see that `ApprovedBy # {}` is not `ApprovedBy = Departments`. A one-token mismatch between a rule
the statement is obliged to state completely and the guard that implements it.

That is structural, and I think it is unfixable inside column C as currently designed:

- §3.2 requires the statement to fix the SYSTEM completely and unambiguously.
- A critique problem asks what the spec fails to say about that system.
- So the answer is a diff between a complete prose spec and an incomplete formal one.

There is nowhere for the gap to hide. Weakening a guard, deleting a check and omitting a rule all
surface the same way. `tla-x8s`'s cfg-tiling route is a second path to the same place, not the
only one.

**The pilot also found where column C's difficulty does live, and that is the part worth
building on.** All three critics spent roughly 80% of their time on the second gap, which cannot
be expressed over the observation operator at all. They proved it three different ways: a
refinement check under a mapping with a negative control, a projected state-graph diff plus a
second independently-written correct spec, and a stuttering simulation with exhaustive
enumeration. Same conclusion, genuinely different instruments.

That is the diversity §6's spread rule looks for. It showed up in the verification method rather
than in the answer, and the rule as written cannot see it.

Redesign I would back: make expressibility the explicit task. Not "what does this spec fail to
say" but "here is a requirement, can it be stated over this interface, and show your work".
Locating a gap is a diff. Deciding whether a requirement is expressible is modeling judgement,
and it is the thing all three critics found hard.

Found running the tla-kl5.11 pilot, step 6.

title: The puzzle screen has no triviality row, so passing it is not evidence of difficulty
description:
§5.7b's rubric asks whether a candidate is the right KIND of thing. No question asks whether the
thing is hard.

The pilot problem scores seven of eight system rows on two independent screens, and agent D
expects all three blind critics to find its primary gap by a route that reads no action bodies.
Both are true at once, because nothing in the eight questions measures difficulty.

That matters more here than it would elsewhere. v1 died of triviality while its own quality gate
passed, and the post-mortem says the gate caused the failure it was written to prevent. A screen
that certifies kind but not difficulty is the same shape of instrument.

I am not asking for a difficulty score. Ask for a route: what is the shortest path to the answer,
and does it exercise the skill the problem claims to teach. Agent D derived exactly that for the
pilot without being asked, so the question is answerable by the agent already doing the screening.

title: A critique problem's .cfg names its own gaps
description:
Agent D found the shortest route through the pilot problem, and it reads no action bodies at all.

The deficient spec declares six named checks. The statement has seven numbered rules. Four rules
are constraint-shaped, two of those carry checks, and the two that carry none are exactly the two
seeded gaps. `diff frozen/PermitReview.cfg statement/PermitReview.cfg` removes precisely
`IssuedOnlyWhenUnanimous` and `AmendmentClearsApprovals`. A critic tabulates rules against
declared checks and reads off both holes.

**This is structural, not a wording defect. The route lives in the `.cfg`, not the prose**, so no
statement rewrite closes it. Any column-C problem built by deleting checks from a complete
reference has it, and Stage 5 authors eight of them.

Three ways out, none tried:

1. Seed a gap as a check that is present but too weak.
2. Break the one-to-one between rules and checks in the reference.
3. Accept it, and put column C's difficulty somewhere other than locating the gap.

Option 1 looks strongest and costs nothing at authoring time. A too-weak check also resembles what
a deficient spec looks like in the wild, which outright deletion does not. Real specs rarely omit
a property; they state a weaker one.

Found running the tla-kl5.11 pilot.

title: A structureless spec grades clean, because every obligation is a one-state predicate
description:
REPRODUCED, and the diagnosis in the title is WRONG. Corrected here rather than in the title so
the history stays legible.

**Lying is not necessary.** A submission with a maximally HONEST operator passes. `chaos-
observations`: `VARIABLE obs`, `Observe == [level |-> obs]` (the variable IS the observation),
`Init == obs \in 0..3`, `Next == obs' \in 0..3`. No transitions, no ordering, no causality,
nothing resembling a lockbox. Against the SHIPPED reference fixture
`harness/fixtures/grade/lockbox/reference`, verified byte-identical by md5:

  verdict PASS, rc=0, Adequacy 2/2, Relational 1/1, NonVacuity PASS, witnesses {}

Central re-ran that independently and got the same object.

**Root cause.** `grade.sh:359-360` emits `SPECIFICATION Spec` and `INVARIANT GRADE_OBLIGATION`,
never `PROPERTY`. So every reference obligation is a SINGLE-STATE PREDICATE over one observation,
and no such predicate can constrain a transition relation. The maximally-permissive spec whose
reachable observation set equals the invariant-admissible set passes BY CONSTRUCTION, for any
reference. A lying operator is one route in. Chaos over honest observations is another, and needs
no lie.

**So this bead and `tla-59s` are the same defect.** `tla-59s` says a temporal obligation cannot be
expressed. This bead is the consequence: because it cannot, a structureless spec grades clean.
Fixing one fixes the other. Dependency added.

**The literal reading in the original title does NOT pass**, which is worth recording. A constant
`Observe` returns INVALID / CONFIG_ERROR rc=3, because the non-vacuity probe `Observe # Observe`
constant-folds. That is an ACCIDENTAL defence, and `grade.sh:465-472`'s stated reason for it is
wrong: it claims the detour "makes it state-dependent, which TLC cannot constant-fold", true only
when the SUBMISSION's operator is state-dependent, which the submission controls.

## What does not close it, measured rather than argued

- **Mandating submission obligations.** Relational checks `PHI => psi_j` against the REFERENCE's
  states with the REFERENCE's operator (`grade.sh:521`). The submitted machine is absent from that
  check, so any statement true of the reference is free to make. Measured PASS rc=0.
- **Landmarks.** They catch exactly one thing, a frozen observation, and only with two or more
  mutually unsatisfiable landmarks. They catch nothing about transition structure.
- **History in the observation.** The strongest thing a reference author can do today. A chaos spec
  restricted to step-admissible PAIRS satisfies a per-state history requirement while the history
  field bears no relation to actual history. Measured PASS rc=0.

## Proposal, measured

Let the reference state TWO-STATE obligations. A `Step_*(o, p)` prefix beside `Req_*` and
`Landmark_*`, judged as

    GRADE_OBLIGATION == [][Step_k(Observe, Observe')]_Observe

declared as `PROPERTY`, MET at rc=0 and UNMET at rc=13.

Measured on `Step_onestep(o,p) == p.level - o.level \in {-1,0,1}`: both attacks caught at rc=13,
both honest submissions pass at rc=0 at two different representations.

**The `_Observe` subscript also answers `tla-nyrb`.** Under `_vars`, a decide-then-commit spec
fails a strict step obligation that a coarse spec passes, which reproduces that bead's
spec-dependence exactly. Under `_Observe` both pass, because a step moving internal state without
moving the observation is a stutter on `Observe` and is excluded by construction. Strict
improvement on the pilot's form.

Not §3.5 reference comparison: `Step_k` is an authored obligation over observations, the same class
of object as `Req_k`, checked against the SUBMISSION. The reference spec is never involved.

## What the proposal does NOT close, and this is the part not to skip

`[][A]_Observe` unfolds to `A \/ UNCHANGED Observe`, so a FROZEN operator satisfies it vacuously.
That is the frozen-mapping trapdoor from the TLAiBench survey §6, reappearing inside the fix.
Measured: a frozen observation returns OK rc=0 against the strict step obligation.

The guard already exists and it is the drawer's own prescription of running the probe alongside
rather than instead: **the landmark suite is the frozen-mapping probe.** So the proposal carries a
hard authoring rule, and per gate-don't-advise it must be a CHECK and not a header note:

  An obligation module stating any Step_* MUST state two or more landmarks with mutually
  unsatisfiable observations.

Cheap and static: count the landmarks, verify pairwise unsatisfiability with one TLC run over the
obligation module alone.

Still open even then: `Step_k` constrains consecutive observations, so a submission can get the
MULTI-step structure wrong while every single step is legal. Smaller hole, not no hole.

## Costs

One TLC run per `Step_k`, and liveness checking is materially dearer than invariant checking, so
the 60s default needs review per problem. `classify` must learn rc=13 (currently falls to
`die_harness`). `run_judge` must emit `PROPERTY` for this form. `Gate!InvariantConfigured` does not
guard a `PROPERTY` cfg — `Gate.tla:68 RefinementConfigured` already does, and `Gate.tla` is
centrally owned, so that part is a central edit.

title: V2-PLAN §5.1's rc table is 6 codes short and the verdict channel has untested branches
description:
`tla-syn` found V2-PLAN.md §5.1's exit-code table was **six codes short**, read straight from the
pinned jar's own enum rather than inferred:

    javap -cp ~/lib/tla2tools.jar -constants 'tlc2.output.EC$ExitStatus'

Missing: `VIOLATION_ASSERT=14`, `FAILURE_SPEC_EVAL=75`, `FAILURE_SAFETY_EVAL=76`,
`FAILURE_LIVENESS_EVAL=77`, `ERROR_STATESPACE_TOO_LARGE=152`, `ERROR_SYSTEM=153`.

`harness/test-verdict.sh` gates 9 codes and none of these six. **The verdict channel every other
harness component depends on has untested branches.**

**rc=75 IS LIVE**, not hypothetical: `puzzles/T29-unchanged/solution/Clock_buggy.tla` exits 75
with "Successor state is not completely specified by action Tick" (central reproduced). Before
the rewire it was classified `PASS-VIOLATION` only because it matched the `Trace exploration`
line of the `*_TTrace_*.tla` file TLC emits alongside the error — and `-noGenerateSpecTE`
suppresses that file, so the canonical invocation would have silently removed the sole basis for
the verdict.

DO, IN THIS ORDER (the RED matters — these are new branches, not a refactor):

1. **Fixtures + assertions in `harness/test-verdict.sh`** for each code you can provoke. 14 and
   75 are straightforward (a failing `Assert`; T29's `Clock_buggy` shape — copy, do not modify
   `puzzles/`). 152 needs a state space over the limit and may be slow — if it costs more than it
   is worth, say so and skip it rather than writing a fixture that does not really provoke it.
   153 may not be provokable at all.
2. **Only map what you measured.** `tla-syn` deliberately left 76 and 77 unmapped because no
   fixture provokes them; a mapping nobody has measured is a guess wearing a table's authority.
   Keep that discipline.
3. **A CENTRAL DECISION IS PENDING and you should surface a recommendation, not decide alone:**
   should 75 get its own verdict token in `harness/verdict.sh`? `tla-syn` mapped it to v1's
   `PASS-VIOLATION` inside verify-puzzle.sh, which preserves v1 intent (T29 exists to demonstrate
   an under-constrained action), but 75 is a *spec evaluation failure*, not a property violation —
   arguably `SPEC_EVAL_FAILURE` deserves its own token so a learner hears "your spec did not
   evaluate" rather than "your property was violated".
4. **Then update V2-PLAN.md §5.1** with the full table and the provenance (the javap command),
   the T29 story, and the note that 76/77 stay unmapped pending measurement.

acceptance_criteria: test-verdict.sh gates every provokable code; unprovokable ones documented as such; §5.1 carries the full table with its javap provenance; the rc=75 token question has a recommendation.
close_reason: Merged to main as 9dbf2ed. Assertions 292 to 298; test-verdict.sh 21 to 27; gate green at 153s. FOUR of the six missing codes were provokable, not two — the worker disassembled errorConstantToExitStatus to find which EC constants route to 76 and 77 (TLC_INVARIANT_EVALUATION_FAILED 2111, TLC_LIVE_FORMULA_TAUTOLOGY 2253), which tla-syn had left unmapped for want of a fixture. 152/153 are NOT hard to provoke, they are DEAD CONSTANTS never emitted: no bytecode in any of the jar's 1394 classes pushes them as an exit value, and they are absent from the enum's own knownExitValues. test-verdict.sh now gates their ABSENCE from verdict.sh, so 'only map what you measured' is enforced rather than advised. TWO FINDINGS CONTRADICTING A NATURAL READING OF THE TABLE: rc=14 is a TIMING fact not a construct fact, and rc=75 is a FAMILY (EC 2103/2109/2115/2147 all route to it). CENTRAL RE-TESTED THE TIMING CLAIM WITH PLACEMENT AS THE ONLY VARIABLE and confirmed it — Assert(FALSE) gives rc=75 in Init and rc=14 in Next — because initial-state computation wraps the EvalException as TLC_NESTED_EXPRESSION. Note the shipped fixture pair does NOT isolate that variable (AssertViolation uses Assert(x < 2) while AssertInInit uses Assert(FALSE)), so the pair demonstrates the rc difference without proving placement causes it; the finding is correct but the fixtures under-support it. THE rc=75 TOKEN DECISION went to its own token: 12/13 mean 'the property was checked and is false, there is a counterexample' while 75 means 'the check never ran', so telling a learner who forgot an UNCHANGED that their property was violated is a false statement about a check that never happened — and collapsing 75 at the measurement layer would push pedagogical judgement into the channel meant to be free of it, the exact inversion tla-kl5.4 removed. Verdict preservation was checked before implementing: verify-puzzle.sh branches on raw rc, not the token, so T29 stays PASS-VIOLATION. verdict.sh touched under this bead's explicit exception, reported loudly.

title: CI runs none of the 8 v2 harness suites — wire the workflows to scripts/cibuild
description:
`.github/workflows/` does not call `scripts/cibuild`. `verify-puzzles.yml` runs only
`scripts/test-verify-puzzle.sh` plus the v1 corpus sweep. **None of the eight v2 harness suites
and no lint run in CI today** — that is 292 assertions and a shellcheck gate that exist, pass
locally, and are invisible to every push and PR.

This is the gate-don't-advise rule failing one level up from where tla-xme fixed it. tla-xme made
`scripts/test` real; this bead makes CI actually call it. Until then the suites are a thing
someone has to remember to run, which is precisely the latent rot surface the rule names.

`scripts/cibuild` already exists and is the intended entry point: pin check, lint, test, docs
build, puzzle corpus, fail-fast. Its phase 1 correctly catches a local/CI TLC mismatch.

CAUTION: `scripts/lint` is RED today (see the sibling bead). Wiring cibuild into CI without
either fixing lint or staging it non-blocking will turn CI red on the first push. Decide which:
fix lint first, or land cibuild with lint advisory and a follow-up to make it blocking. Do NOT
silently drop lint from cibuild to get green — that recreates the problem this bead exists to fix.

title: Stage 3 §6 — one pilot problem through all 8 steps and 4 gates
description:
AUTOFAN-EXCLUDE: attended — this bead IS the barrier that exists to prevent fan-out. Run it alone.

Goal: run exactly ONE problem through the full eight-step, four-gate pipeline before any fan-out.
Find the breakages on one problem, not forty.

PICK THE PILOT FROM GAP #11 — critique exercises, "what does this spec fail to say?". Cheapest to
author, no public prior art anywhere in TLA+ pedagogy, and it exercises the grading engine
without needing refinement. Grid cell: task shape C.

PIPELINE (§6), agent briefs in §9.4–§9.9:
  1  Write reference COLD — optimized only as a spec, no commentary      agent A  §9.4
  2  Verify: properties pass, vacuity probes fail correctly,
     seeded variants caught                                             agent B  §9.5  [all green]
  3  Freeze + hash                                                      central, inline [hash recorded]
  4  Write statement FROM the frozen spec                               agent C  §9.6
  5  Leakage check — adversarial, separate agent                        agent D  §9.7  [nothing leaked]
  6  Blind solve ×3 — fresh agents, statement only                      agents E1-E3 §9.8 [spread rules]
  7  Comment pass — frozen spec, comments only                          agent F  §9.9
  8  Strip-and-diff gate                                                central, inline [byte-identical
                                                                                        modulo comments]

READING THE BLIND-SOLVE SPREAD (step 6) — this is the measurement; do not soften it:
  - ALL THREE FAIL → underspecified, or requires knowledge outside learntla core. Fix the statement.
  - ALL THREE SUCCEED FIRST-TRY WITH NEAR-IDENTICAL STRUCTURE → TRIVIAL, or the statement is
    LEAKING. This is a FAILURE, not a pass. Send back to step 4.
  - ALL THREE SUCCEED WITH GENUINELY DIFFERENT STATE REPRESENTATIONS → TARGET ACHIEVED. This is
    the measurable proxy for "admits real modeling choice".
  - MIXED → read the telemetry: attempts taken, whether TLC caught bugs in the first draft,
    whether the solver revised its state representation.
A first-try clean solve from every solver ALWAYS flags for human review.

ISOLATION IS STRUCTURAL, NOT INSTRUCTIONAL (§0, §6b.1). A blind solver is only a valid instrument
if it genuinely has not seen the reference — fresh agent, minimal brief, no shared context. Never
shortcut a gate by doing the work inline; the gate IS the isolation.

Note from §5.8: TLAiBench's ten puzzles are in LLM training data, so blind solvers will have
memorized them. Do not pick anything adjacent to them for the pilot.

title: Stage 2 §5.4 — refinement checking, with the frozen-mapping trapdoor closed
description:
Goal: refinement checking that cannot be passed by a mapping which proves nothing.

IDIOM: define `Refines == Abstract!Spec` in the module; the .cfg gets SPECIFICATION Spec
(concrete) + PROPERTY Refines. The .cfg accepts ONLY BARE IDENTIFIERS — `PROPERTY A!Spec` fails
with a misleading message about A, which will cost an hour if you have not been warned.

THE PROBE — mandatory on every refinement problem. Name the mapped expression, assert as an
ORDINARY INVARIANT that it never leaves its initial value, and require TLC to VIOLATE it:

  SPECIFICATION Spec
  PROPERTY  Refines
  INVARIANT Probe        \* MappedExpr = <initial value>

A PASSING PROBE IS A FAILING REFINEMENT CHECK. If TLC cannot violate Probe, the mapping is
frozen and the refinement proved nothing. Why: [][ANext]_(mapped) unfolds to
ANext \/ UNCHANGED(mapped), so a frozen mapping makes the right disjunct true at every step and
ANext is never evaluated once. Verified — a concrete spec with three interleaving actions and 27
distinct states passes at rc=0.

GRADING CONSEQUENCE of Lamport's caveat (§4.4 item 9 — for ANY two specs, suitable auxiliary
variables make a mapping exist, so "X refines Y" is a fact about X, Y AND the mapping): WE supply
the mapping and grade only the concrete spec. Where the mapping is itself the exercise, grade by
probe + inspection, NEVER by TLC's verdict alone.

Other verified traps:
  - omitting WITH is SILENT — implicit same-name substitution gives a different, usually wrong
    mapping that passes
  - the abstract's `vars` tuple is substituted too
  - (§10) `THEOREM Spec => A!Spec` DOES NOTHING. TLC silently ignores THEOREM; it is TLAPS
    documentation. Verified: a deliberately wrong concrete spec with a THEOREM and no PROPERTY
    returns "No error has been found". Reject any submission whose refinement claim lives only
    in a THEOREM.
  - (§10) SYMMETRY and VIEW make temporal checking UNSOUND — SS p.244/246: may "miss errors,
    report an error that doesn't exist, or report a real error with an incorrect counterexample."
    No symmetry on any problem checking a temporal property, and refinement IS one.

Files: harness/refinement.sh

RED: GIVEN a concrete spec with a FROZEN refinement mapping — one that never leaves its initial
value — WHEN refinement.sh runs, THEN it FAILS the submission, even though TLC's own
PROPERTY Refines check exits 0.
acceptance_criteria: Probe enforced on every refinement invocation; THEOREM-only claims rejected; SYMMETRY refused when a temporal property is checked; missing-WITH either detected or explicitly documented as out of scope.
notes:
DESIGN UNCHANGED AND NOW EMPIRICALLY VINDICATED (tla-kl5.3 survey, drawer_tla_puzzles_decisions_6251f5ad5930c77a531e9917). TLAiBench — the only public TLA+ benchmark grading refinement — has the frozen-mapping trapdoor WIDE OPEN. A fully frozen mapping (WITH big <- 0, small <- 0) passes its plain refinement check AND its Gold!Refinement postcondition at rc=0, while our INVARIANT Probe cleanly separates frozen (rc=0 -> fail) from correct (rc=12 -> pass), re-verified on TLC 2026.07.31 — a newer build than §5 was written against. Its Gold!Stats discriminates NOTHING about the mapping: it rejects correct and frozen alike on an unrelated diameter mismatch. State the probe's importance more strongly than 'a trap we noticed'.

ADD, alongside the probe and never instead of it: RefinementConfigured == TLCGet('spec').impliedinits # {} /\ TLCGet('spec').impliedactions # {} (adapted from gold/DieHardGold.tla:137-141, MIT (c) 2025 TLA+ Foundation — attribute in a comment). Disjoint coverage: no PROPERTY in the cfg -> guard fires, probe silent. PROPERTY present but mapping frozen -> guard silent, probe fires.

DO NOT COPY TLAiBench's CONFIG OWNERSHIP: it lets the subject under evaluation author its own .cfg, which is HOW the trapdoor stays open. Our .cfg stays harness-owned.
FILES CORRECTION: harness/Gate.tla is CENTRALLY OWNED and already on main, carrying RefinementConfigured (verified rc=10 with no PROPERTY line, rc=0 with one). Your footprint is harness/refinement.sh + harness/fixtures/refinement/ ONLY. Treat Gate.tla as read-only — tla-kl5.6 consumes it in parallel with you.
close_reason: harness/refinement.sh + 28 fixtures, merged to main; plan correction in commit 73dca11. 43 assertions green alongside all siblings. Found a real defect in V2-PLAN.md section 5.4, independently reproduced by central: the .cfg as the plan drew it (SPECIFICATION + PROPERTY + INVARIANT together) CANNOT certify a refinement — measured rc=12 with 4 of 7 reachable states, because the invariant violation halts the search before the property is evaluated over the rest. Plan now specifies two separate runs with the guard on run A alone; on run B it fires on run B's own missing PROPERTY and masks the frozen verdict. Also established harness probe ownership is separately load-bearing. Corpus pass over the 7 refinement puzzles surfaced tla-qut.

title: Stage 2 §5.2 — grading engine: conjunct-wise two-sided implication + non-vacuity
description:
Goal: conjunct-wise two-sided implication plus non-vacuity.

REFERENCE-COMPARISON GRADING IS INVALID AND MUST NOT CREEP BACK IN (§3.5): over ~96,000 Alloy
submissions the instructor's oracle ranks #1 among correct forms for only 33% of exercises, and
is ABSENT ENTIRELY in 18.6%. "Compare to the reference" is the intuitive design and it is wrong.

Given student Ψ and reference Φ:
  1. Ψ => φᵢ for each REFERENCE conjunct  → not too weak (this is where per-conjunct partial
                                            credit comes from)
  2. Φ => ψⱼ for each STUDENT conjunct    → not too strong
  3. Ψ => false must FAIL                 → not vacuous

Report over-constraint and under-constraint INDEPENDENTLY, and ALLOW BOTH — 23.6% of wrong models
are both simultaneously, so a design that treats them as exclusive misgrades a quarter of the
failures. Emit one witness of each.

Include a `Relational` suite that rejects specs which are TOO STRICT. Over-constraining is the
sin that reference-comparison grading actively teaches, and it dominates in the measured data.

Output is a VERDICT OBJECT — never a diff, never reference conjuncts. A grader that says "you're
missing conjunct 3 of the reference" leaks the decomposition (§6b.2). Feedback is error LOCATION
only (§3.7, the only RCT on the question): location hints 9.12 tasks vs 5.67 control;
counterexample hints statistically INDISTINGUISHABLE from no hint; natural-language description
hints BELOW control and the most demoralizing arm. Nothing improved retention. Prettifying a
trace is not an improvement — it is the arm that measured as worthless.

Files: harness/grade.sh

RED: GIVEN a reference Φ and a student spec Ψ that is simultaneously too strong on one conjunct
and too weak on another, WHEN grade.sh runs, THEN it reports BOTH an over-constraint witness and
an under-constraint witness, and the verdict object contains no reference conjunct text.
acceptance_criteria: All three obligations implemented; the both-at-once case covered by a test; verdict-object schema documented and leak-free.
notes: FROM THE tla-kl5.3 SURVEY (drawer_tla_puzzles_decisions_6251f5ad5930c77a531e9917): design UNCHANGED, add one citation. TLAiBench grades by whole-spec refinement against a gold reference, which is one-sided and STRUCTURALLY BLIND TO OVER-CONSTRAINT — an over-constrained spec still refines gold, and the maximally over-constrained spec (unsatisfiable Init) refines everything (verified rc=0 on both the plain check and Gold!Refinement). That is the sin §5.2 says dominates the data. Cite TLAiBench commit ba95443 'Validation: Relax state-space statistics' in the code rationale: its Gold!Stats originally demanded the submission's state space equal the reference's NUMERICALLY (generated=97, distinct=16 — exactly the gold spec's own figures) and was relaxed in the field within hours. That is third-party corroboration of §3.5 from the benchmark author himself. One idea worth adapting: their phase-2 'rc==12 required' gate is our -inv FALSE smoke test in disguise, free from the puzzle framing — but it does NOT transfer to §5.7b system problems, where no counterexample is expected.
close_reason: harness/grade.sh, merged to main; plan corrections in commit 73dca11. 57 assertions green on merged main alongside all sibling suites. Conjunct-wise two-sided implication over a variable-free observation record — that phrasing is what makes cross-checking possible when reference and submission have unrelated representations, not a style choice. Relational suite has TWO members: the declared over-constraint check plus a landmark-reachability refutation catching over-constraint BY OMISSION, the form learners actually produce. Leak gate is whitelist and fail-closed, mutation-proven to bite. Found a gap now recorded in V2-PLAN.md section 5.3: INVARIANT FALSE in a .cfg is rejected at rc=151 because TLC constant-folds before search, while the CLI form tlc -inv FALSE works at rc=12 — central verified both routes.

title: Stage 2 §5.3 — vacuity probes: the rc=0 trap that deadlock checking does not catch
description:
Goal: close the trap where a spec that models NOTHING scores full marks.

THE TRAP: an unsatisfiable Init yields "No error has been found", "0 states generated", and
rc=0. DEADLOCK CHECKING DOES NOT CATCH IT. Every problem needs a vacuity gate or vacuous
submissions pass silently.

CHEAP SMOKE TEST: `tlc -inv "FALSE" Learner.tla`.
  rc=12 → reachable states exist (GOOD);  rc=0 → the space is EMPTY (VACUOUS).
No file edits needed, and it evaluates in the learner's namespace. The injected invariant is
auto-named __DebuggerExpr__<nanotime> — NEVER pattern-match that name.

REAL GATE: -postCondition "Gate!NonVacuous" with TLCGet("distinct") >= N. It MUST live in a
separate module or you get "Circular dependency among .tla files". Verified to fire correctly
even at 0 initial states.

  ---- MODULE Gate ----
  EXTENDS Naturals, TLC
  NonVacuous == TLCGet("distinct") >= 4
  ====

DEAD-ACTION DETECTION via -coverage 1: the predicate is `total == 0`, NEVER `distinct == 0`. An
action can fire and discover nothing new — PlusCal's generated Terminating shows 0:1 on EVERY
terminating spec (verified on the real puzzles/T01-the-light-switch solution), so keying on
distinct produces a false positive on essentially every PlusCal submission. The indented
sub-counts localize WHERE an action died, which is what turns feedback into "your guard x > 100
is never true" instead of "unreachable" — and error location is the only feedback form that
measured as working (§3.7).

Files: harness/vacuity.sh, harness/Gate.tla

RED: GIVEN a spec whose Init is unsatisfiable, WHEN vacuity.sh runs, THEN it returns VACUOUS —
even though a bare TLC run on that same spec exits 0 with "No error has been found".
acceptance_criteria: Smoke test + postCondition gate + dead-action detection implemented; Gate.tla is a separate module; the dead-action predicate is total==0; T01's Terminating 0:1 produces no false positive.
notes:
TWO ADDITIONS, both verified on TLC 2026.03.04.183147.

(1) A SECOND VACUITY VECTOR, found while building tla-kl5.4 and NOT in the original plan. A .cfg keyword with no operand is not an error: 'SPECIFICATION Spec' + a bare 'INVARIANT' line makes TLC report 'Model checking completed. No error has been found.' at rc=0, having checked NO invariant at all. THE GATE IN THIS BEAD DOES NOT CATCH IT — the state space is perfectly healthy (3 distinct states in the reproduction), so TLCGet('distinct') >= N passes. It is not the state space that is empty, it is the CHECKING. Mechanical guard, verified rc=10 on the dangling keyword and rc=0 on a real invariant: InvariantConfigured == TLCGet('spec').invariants # {}.

(2) STEAL TLAiBench's configuration guard (drawer ...6251f5ad5930c77a531e9917): RefinementConfigured == TLCGet('spec').impliedinits # {} /\ TLCGet('spec').impliedactions # {} — adapted from gold/DieHardGold.tla:137-141, MIT (c) 2025 TLA+ Foundation, attribute in a comment. It catches a .cfg that never declared the refinement PROPERTY.

These generalize: treat 'the check was actually configured' as a GUARD FAMILY over TLCGet('spec'), and run the relevant member alongside NonVacuous on every problem. It and NonVacuous catch disjoint failures — an empty state space, versus an empty obligation over a healthy one.

REJECT TLAiBench's exact-equality Stats fingerprint in favor of our >= N threshold; their own relaxation commit is the evidence exact equality does not survive contact. 0-initial-states behavior is identical either way, so no change there. Keep Gate as a SEPARATE module: when the root module is the one holding the operator, -postcondition Module!Op fails with 'Parsing or semantic analysis failed'.
FILES CORRECTION: harness/Gate.tla is now CENTRALLY OWNED and already on main (all three guards written and verified). Your footprint is harness/vacuity.sh + harness/fixtures/vacuity/ ONLY. Treat Gate.tla as read-only — tla-kl5.7 consumes it in parallel with you, and it is the one file you would both otherwise write. If you need the NonVacuous threshold parameterized per-problem, do that in vacuity.sh, not by editing Gate.tla.
close_reason: harness/vacuity.sh + test-vacuity.sh, merged to main; plan corrections in commit 73dca11. 26 assertions green alongside all siblings. Distinguishes three vacuity vectors with distinct tokens and exit codes because each needs different remediation. Central verified the headline claim: Gate!NonVacuous returns rc=0 on the dangling-INVARIANT fixture, the miss this bead closes. Worker further established the guards are disjoint in BOTH directions — InvariantConfigured returns rc=0 on the empty-Init spec — so neither subsumes the other and dropping either opens a hole. total==0 predicate mutation-verified against the PlusCal Terminating 0:1 false positive. Surfaced the SIGPIPE structural-assertion bug now tracked as tla-kr9.

title: Stage 2 §5.8 — read TLAiBench first and record what to steal

title: Stage 2 §5.1 — verdict channel: exit codes, never stdout greps
description:
Goal: every harness component branches on TLC's EXIT CODE, never on grepping stdout. This is the
foundation the other seven components sit on, so it lands first and they depend on it.

Verified rc table (TLC 2026.03.04 / tla2tools 1.8.0 — do not re-derive; do re-verify if you
change TLC versions):
    0  success
   10  ASSUME or -postCondition false
   11  deadlock
   12  safety violation (INVARIANT)
   13  liveness / action-property violation (PROPERTY, incl. refinement)
  150  parse / semantic failure
  151  config failure
  255  file not found
Wrap in `timeout` and treat rc=124 as its own verdict.

Canonical invocation (§5.1):
  tlc -workers 1 -deadlock -noGenerateSpecTE -nowarning \
      -coverage 1 -dumpTrace json trace.json \
      -postCondition "Gate!NonVacuous" \
      -metadir "$SCRATCH/states" Harness.tla -config Harness.cfg

-workers 1 IS MANDATORY. Counterexamples are nondeterministic above one worker — five runs at
-workers 8 gave three different traces. State COUNTS are stable and safe to publish (measured
identical across workers 1/4/8, three fingerprint polynomials, and TLC 2.15 → 2026.03.04), so
the constraint bites only where a TRACE is the output. Record that distinction in the file;
someone will otherwise "optimize" the worker count back.

Files: harness/verdict.sh, harness/test-verdict.sh

RED: INVARIANT: for each rc in {0,10,11,12,13,150,151,255,124} a purpose-built fixture spec
drives verdict.sh to exactly that verdict, and no verdict is ever derived from stdout text.
acceptance_criteria: A fixture per rc, all passing; -workers 1 pinned in the canonical invocation; no grep of TLC stdout anywhere in the file.

title: Stage 1 §4 — author the refinement chapter
description:
Goal: a chapter teaching refinement in TLA+, pitched as a direct continuation of learntla.com's
core section — same register, same assumed background, same voice. learntla's own
topics/refinement is a STUB (its topics index says outright "Most of the topics haven't been
written yet"), so this fills a hole the upstream site advertises.

THESIS (§4.1 — Frank's, and it is well supported): refinement is the technique that makes
modeling large and complex systems tractable, not a formalism to be admired. Supporting
evidence to use:
  - Lamport & Merz, Prophecy Made Simple §5: rather than adding prophecy variables to Afek's
    snapshot algorithm they INVENT AN INTERMEDIATE SPEC, so one link needs only history
    variables and the other needs prophecy on a simple spec. Their justification: "the
    specification of what an algorithm is supposed to do is generally much simpler than the
    algorithm."
  - ewd998/EWD998ChanID.cfg chains three instance hops (EWD998Chan!EWD998!TD!Live) —
    transitivity as practiced.
  - Properties proved of the abstract transfer to the concrete for free.
HONEST COUNTERWEIGHT, must be included: Lamport (SS §10.9) says that when writing from scratch a
monolithic spec is usually easier to understand. The chapter says refinement earns its keep when
the system exceeds what you can hold in one spec — NOT that it is always better.

DO NOT RE-TEACH (§4.2). Core ch.13 already teaches INSTANCE, INSTANCE..WITH, constant and
variable substitution, EXTENDS vs INSTANCE, partial parameterization. Core ch.12 teaches vars,
Init, Next, actions, primed variables, UNCHANGED, Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars, stuttering via
[A]_v, ENABLED, and formal WF/SF — but to READING depth, as a bridge from PlusCal. The gap is
narrow: the IDEA that a concrete spec implements an abstract one, refinement mappings, and the
Spec => Abstract!Spec check.

CUT LIST §4.3 — dense notation, easy idea:
  \EE / ∃∃ (Lamport calls it the stone in the soup; neither TLC nor TLAPS handles it — present
  once for meaning, never for use) · the LM!Inner(omem, octl, obuf)!ISpec chains from SS §5.8 ·
  the overbar F̄ (it means "substitute"; say "substitute") · parametrized instantiation
  Inner(q) == INSTANCE InnerFIFO (Lamport himself: "If this seems confusing, don't worry about
  it") · Prophecy.tla's general machinery (ProphAction, ProphCondition, DomInj, PredDom) — use
  PMS §4.2's three-line recipe instead · Abadi & Lamport's Σ,F,N,L tuples and structured proofs.

SLOW-DOWN LIST §4.4 — genuinely hard, all nine:
  1. Stuttering as CONSTITUTIVE, not permissive. A spec describes part of a world; that alone
     forces [...]_vars. Refinement then gets stuttering for free.
  2. THE VACUITY HOLE — make this the CENTREPIECE of the stuttering section, not a footnote.
     [][ANext]_(mapped) unfolds to ANext \/ UNCHANGED(mapped), so a frozen mapping makes the
     right disjunct true at every step and ANext is never evaluated once. Verified: a concrete
     spec with three interleaving actions and 27 distinct states passes at rc=0. Stuttering is
     both the load-bearing beam and the trapdoor.
  3. The vars-substitution consequence — the abstract's stuttering subscript is itself rewritten
     by the mapping, determining which concrete steps are invisible. Almost never stated.
  4. Why refinement mappings can FAIL TO EXIST — Abadi & Lamport's three counterexamples.
  5. Prophecy variables. Unlock: PMS §4.3 — "a specification is not a rule for generating
     behaviors. It's a predicate on behaviors." Get that sentence in EARLY.
  6. The non-constraining obligation — an equivalence, not an implication. History variables get
     it free (syntactic); prophecy variables must earn it.
  7. ENABLED not distributing over substitution — what makes liveness refinement hard.
  8. Machine closure, and prophecy's interaction with it.
  9. "Refinement is a claim about THREE things, not two." From Hiding §5: for ANY two specs,
     adding suitable auxiliary variables makes a mapping exist, so "X refines Y" is a fact about
     X, Y, AND THE MAPPING. PUT THIS NEAR THE BEGINNING, not the last page.

OPEN DETAIL TO SETTLE FIRST (§2.3): total length, and whether this ships as one document or as
chapter + separate worked example. Everything else in §2.3 is approved.

Brief: V2-PLAN.md §9.1 — copy-paste it.

Files: chapter/refinement.md, chapter/snippets/

Steps:
  1. Settle the §2.3 length/format detail with Frank.
  2. Dispatch the §9.1 author brief to an isolated agent.
  3. Every TLA+ snippet lands in chapter/snippets/ as a runnable .tla + .cfg pair — execution is
     verified by the sibling bead, but this bead must make them runnable in the first place.
acceptance_criteria: chapter/refinement.md exists; covers all 9 §4.4 slow-down items and none of the §4.3 cut list; every snippet has a runnable pair in chapter/snippets/.

All 26 snippets execute green on TLC 2026.03.04.183147 via chapter/snippets/run-all.sh. All nine section 4.4 slow-down items placed, with the two mandated positions honored: 'a claim about three things' is section 3, and the vacuity hole is the spine of both documents. Every quotation traced to a clone or a local pdftotext extraction, none from WebFetch. title: [epic] v2 implementation: refinement chapter, harness, pilot, tutor directory, batched production
description:
Implementation epic for the v2 rebuild. Spawned from V2-PLAN.md (bead tla-qpm) on 2026-08-06.

V2-PLAN.md is the execution plan and the source of truth for every child here; each child cites
its section. READ V2-PLAN.md §1 AND §3 BEFORE WORKING ANY CHILD — §3 is a list of decisions that
are CLOSED, and reopening one wastes a session and usually re-derives a worse answer, because
most were settled against measured evidence rather than intuition.

Six stages, ordered by dependency:

  Stage 1  §4   refinement chapter        no deps — start now
  Stage 2  §5   harness, 8 components     no deps — start now, parallel with Stage 1
  Stage 3  §6   pilot problem end-to-end  needs Stage 2
  Stage 4  §6b  tutor directory           needs Stage 2 + Stage 3
  Stage 5  §7   batched production        needs Stage 3 + Stage 4
  Stage 6  §8   assembly                  needs Stage 5

Copy-pasteable subagent briefs for every unit are in V2-PLAN.md §9.

WHY SUBAGENTS SPECIFICALLY — isolation is load-bearing, not just parallelism (§0):
  - a BLIND SOLVER is only a valid instrument if it genuinely has not seen the reference; a
    fresh agent with a minimal brief guarantees that and a same-context continuation cannot
  - the COMMENT PASS must not be able to reshape the spec it is annotating
  - the LEAKAGE CHECK must be adversarial against a statement its author is attached to
Treat "spawn a fresh agent" as the enforcement mechanism for these gates. Never shortcut one by
doing the work inline.

LAYOUT settled 2026-08-06: harness/ and chapter/ are NEW top-level dirs in this repo. v1's
puzzles/ and scripts/ are untouched. tla-practice/ and tla-answers/ (§6b.2) split off as
SEPARATE repos at Stage 4 — that separation is a leak defense, not a preference.

Stages 5 and 6 are filed COARSE on purpose. Batch 1's learner telemetry is expected to reshape
them (§7.1), so they get decomposed when the pilot lands, not now.

title: v2 rebuild: consolidate design, author refinement chapter, build harness, then spawn implementation epic
description:
v1's programmed-text microlesson curriculum failed: test questions were trivial or near-copies of the lesson example; lessons were sometimes vacuous or wrong. Post-mortem concluded the failure was STRUCTURAL, not execution — the "exactly one new concept" + minimal-novelty quality gate mechanically produces near-copies. See drawer_tla_puzzles_decisions_78e0afcd8f0f7bb925f61ef0.

v2 replaces the content (not the infrastructure): learntla.com core assumed as read, ~40-60 original modeling problems at 20-40 min each, ~25 of 60 in pure TLA+ back-loaded.

DESIGN IS CAPTURED IN THREE DRAWERS (tla_puzzles/decisions):
  78e0afcd8f0f7bb925f61ef0 — v1 post-mortem
  d6fc1f6386188c44b58278b8 — problem-set contract, production pipeline, exclusion regime
  be8cc4b03efbea276e444a12 — mechanical grading architecture + TLC harness constraints

Design is informed by a four-sweep research pass (2026-08-05): existing TLA+ exercise sets, Lamport refinement extraction, formal-methods pedagogy, and empirically-verified TLC/Apalache tooling capability.

NOT YET DONE — this bead tracks the remaining design-to-build transition:
  - assemble the three drawers into one consolidated design document for human review
  - decide the final problem count and the modeling-situation taxonomy
  - author the refinement chapter (learntla's topics/refinement is a stub; Specifying Systems ch.10-11 rewritten in learntla's register). Cut/slow-down outline is in the refinement research notes.
  - build the harness (vacuity probes, conjunct-wise grading, blind-solve loop, comment-pass gate)
  - THEN spawn the implementation epic via create-beads

KEY CONSTRAINTS not to relitigate:
  - coverage is an end-of-run AUDIT, never the problem-list generator
  - statement fixes the SYSTEM, leaves the REPRESENTATION open, names an observation operator
  - interleave by idiom; never consecutive problems of one kind (d=0.83)
  - reference-comparison grading is invalid (oracle is #1 for only 33% of exercises)
  - mechanical layer decides pass/fail; LLM judge explains only, never overrides
  - comments added in a SEPARATE post-freeze pass, enforced by strip-and-diff
acceptance_criteria: A consolidated v2 design document exists and is human-reviewed; the refinement chapter is drafted; the verification harness runs end-to-end on one pilot problem; an implementation epic is filed.
notes:
NEW SCREEN ADDED 2026-08-06: §5.7b, the puzzle-versus-system screen. It is INDEPENDENT of the §5.7 mechanism-collision screen — §5.7 asks 'has someone already solved this?', §5.7b asks 'is it even the right kind of thing?' A candidate can pass §5.7 cleanly and still be useless.

THE SCREEN: if you hand the learner the legal moves, is there anything left to model? If no, it is a puzzle — cut it, or add agents and failure until it isn't.

WHY IT MATTERS: every puzzle in tlaplus/Examples (Die Hard, Hanoi, N-Queens, missionaries, sliding block) is flagged Beginner — not because they are small but because the modeling was pre-done by whoever wrote the rules. 'Puzzles where the state space is handed to you and the work is search' is the first of the four categories the corpus survey found the entire public corpus consists of, and it is the category this project is defined against.

IMPORTANT NUANCE: local representation choices do NOT rescue a puzzle. Change-ringing genuinely offers some (bells->positions vs positions->bells; explicit visited-row history vs exploiting TLC's own dedup, since a repeated row IS a repeated state). Those are real and interesting, but they are local — about transcribing a given action set tidily, not about deciding what the actions are. Good taste, not modeling judgment.

RESCUE PATTERN: add agents and fallibility, which converts search into specification. Change-ringing as a puzzle is 'find a Hamiltonian path through the Cayley graph of S_n'. As a system it is 'model a band of fallible ringers; does their behaviour refine the method they are attempting?' — which lands in column F.

THE SCREEN HAS TEETH BEYOND CHANGE-RINGING: restaurant seating FAILS as 'seat this party optimally' (bin-packing) and PASSES as 'model the host stand with walk-ins and reservations arriving concurrently'. Same domain, different statement. So the screen is applied at STATEMENT time (§6 step 4, brief §9.6) as well as at domain-selection time — passing once does not immunize a domain.
EPIC FILED 2026-08-06: tla-kl5 (22 children) is the implementation epic this bead's fourth acceptance criterion called for. Stage 1 = tla-kl5.1/.2 (chapter); Stage 2 = tla-kl5.3-.10 (harness); Stage 3 = tla-kl5.11 (pilot); Stage 4 = tla-kl5.12-.15 (tutor directory); Stage 5 = tla-kl5.16/.17 (batch 1 + holdout); Stage 6 = tla-kl5.18-.21 (assembly); tla-kl5.22 = the §11 research gaps. Layout settled at filing time: harness/ and chapter/ are NEW top-level dirs in this repo; tla-practice/ and tla-answers/ split off as separate repos at Stage 4. tla-syn (verify-puzzle.sh rc rewire) now depends on tla-kl5.4, which owns the canonical rc table. title: Lane A is §3.7's control arm, not its worst arm — and §3.7 overreaches its citation
description:
Central filed a handoff hole saying Lane A might be §3.7's worst arm (natural-language description
hints, below control, most demoralizing). **The research audit says that framing is wrong, and the
correction matters.**

The RCT's three arms were hints delivered DURING solving, ABOUT the learner's own error. Lane A's
commented reference differs on all three defining properties: post-attempt not mid-impasse; about
the REFERENCE's decisions not the learner's error; elective reading not interruptive feedback. The
demoralization finding attached to being told in prose what is wrong with your work while stuck.
**Lane A is not the NL arm. In the study's terms it is the CONTROL arm.**

So the cost is not "below control". It is forfeiting the one arm that worked, roughly a 60%
task-completion gain.

**But there is a real compound nobody had written down.** With no grader, the only verdict channel
on Frank's attempt is his own comparison of it to the reference. That is reference-comparison
grading — §3.5's banned method — performed by the least-equipped grader available, in a domain
chosen under §3.10 precisely so he lacks the schema to adjudicate, where §3.5's own data predicts a
correct-but-different form looks wrong most of the time (oracle ranks #1 for 33%, absent in 18.6%).
The output, "mine looks wrong, this felt bad", is what §7.1 says is a reliable AMBIGUITY signal and
an unreliable DIFFICULTY signal. So mis-graded self-comparison masquerades as bug reports and feeds
§7.1's fix-the-broken loop with false positives.

**Zero-cost partial fix:** ship the author's `alternatives.md` (the representations considered and
rejected) WITH the commentary rather than keeping it author-only. It is the one existing artifact
that shows Frank the space of correct-but-different.

**Separately, §3.7 overreaches its own citation.** Its last line is "Nothing improved retention", so
the positive result is an in-practice PERFORMANCE result. By §7.2's own standard, performance during
practice is an unreliable index of learning. §3.7 is sound as harm-avoidance and as UX; as a claim
that location feedback TEACHES, it exceeds what the study shows. The invariant policing feedback
quality rests on the metric class the project disavows.

§3.9: "Every property ships with one satisfying and one violating trace. Multiple positive
instances had no measured effect; negative instances did."

**It has no implementation, no owner and no bead.** The §6 pipeline's steps produce no learner-facing
trace at any point. The pilot shipped PROBLEM.md plus spec plus cfg and nothing else. The three

And the taxonomy table has quietly narrowed it from "every property" to a column-B annotation
(V2-PLAN.md:115 against :271) — scope erosion nobody decided.

It is the only §3 invariant that is pure dead text.

What makes it worth filing rather than shrugging at: its evidential basis is the same
negative-instance logic the project relies on everywhere else — seeded variants, violating
behaviours as evidence. And the machinery already exists: `-dumpTrace json` and `seeded-bugs.sh`.
Honouring it is a per-problem script, not a component.

Decide one of two things and record it: re-own the invariant and add a pipeline step, or formally
narrow it to column B. Right now it cites evidence for a practice nothing performs.

title: Difficulty verdicts do not record which models produced them
description:
Every difficulty judgment this project makes runs through blind solvers, and §2.1's target —
problems that admit real modeling choice — is measured by their spread. Nothing records which
models produced a verdict.

That matters two ways.

**A verdict from one family is a verdict about that family.** The Stage 3 pilot's step 6 used three
instances of one model and returned byte-identical answers. The mixed-panel re-run
(`pilot/reports/step6-mixed-panel.md`) showed the content convergence was real and not a panel
artifact — but it also showed that a three-instance single-model panel returned 0 in 3 on a defect
that the six-critic mixed panel caught at 1 in 6.

**Calibration goes stale silently.** A problem tuned to be hard for today's models may be trivial
for next year's, and nothing in the pipeline would notice. The `tla-03d2` research reached the same
conclusion about its recall probe and prescribed the fix there: record the model id and the date
with the verdict.

Asks:

- Record panel composition — model ids, count per model, date — alongside every step-6 result and
  every difficulty verdict.
- Prefer mixed panels. The measured reason is not that content diverges, because it did not. It is
  that depth of justification does, and depth is what column C grades.
- Re-run the panel when the model set changes, and treat a verdict older than the current model set
  as unverified rather than as passing.
