title: grade.sh appends its constants.cfg unvalidated, the third site of one class
description:
Three harness components build a `.cfg` from a caller-supplied fragment. Two of them now refuse a
directive in that fragment. `grade.sh` does not.

- `refinement.sh --constants` — guard existed but was line-anchored while TLC's parser is
  token-oriented, so `(* c *) SYMMETRY Perms` walked past it. Hardened in `tla-nesz`.
- `seeded-bugs.sh constants.cfg` — validated from the start, added in `tla-40y`, refusing a
  directive as `MATRIX_MALFORMED`.
- **`grade.sh constants.cfg` — appended verbatim, no validation.** `grade.sh:361` is
  `[ -n "$CONST_FRAG" ] && cat "$CONST_FRAG"`, straight into every generated judge `.cfg`.

Two independent agents found the first two on the same day without knowing about each other, which
is why I think this is a class rather than three bugs.

**What it costs here, and it is not the SYMMETRY story.** grade.sh emits `INVARIANT
GRADE_OBLIGATION`, and symmetry reduction on pure invariant checking is sound, so §10's temporal
hazard does not bite directly. The live one is a smuggled second `INVARIANT`: grade.sh reads rc=12
as "the obligation was UNMET", so a second invariant firing is misattributed to the obligation
under test. A `CONSTRAINT` is the other direction — it truncates the reachable space and can turn
an UNMET into a MET.

Threat model is weaker than for the other two, because the reference package is harness-owned
rather than submission-owned. So this is an author-error trap, not an attack surface. That is
still worth closing: §5.7's whole posture is that the `.cfg` stays harness-owned precisely so
grading cannot be weakened, and an author who puts one wrong line in `constants.cfg` gets silently
wrong grades rather than an error.

Fix: reuse `seeded-bugs.sh`'s validator rather than writing a third one. Strip `\*` comments,
match keywords as tokens anywhere rather than line-anchored, refuse anything that is not a
`CONSTANT` or `CONSTANTS` assignment.

Worth checking at the same time whether a fourth site exists. `vacuity.sh` has no constants
channel today, which may itself be a gap, since it cannot drive a parameterized spec either.

title: refinement.sh reports a real refinement failure as SAFETY_VIOLATION
description:
`harness/refinement.sh` RUN A routes rc=13 to `REFINEMENT_VIOLATED` and everything else to a
catch-all that emits the raw verdict token. Central checked the common cases during the pilot and
they route correctly: implied-init and implied-action obligations both exit 13, and so does a
broken fairness conjunct.

The `tla-94n` worker found the case the corrected row-13 predicts. **An abstract spec whose own
`Spec` formula carries a safety-shaped temporal conjunct exits 12.**

Measured: `ASpec == AInit /\ [][ANext]_a /\ [](AHot => []AHot)`, concrete violating the third
conjunct, gives rc=12 `SAFETY_VIOLATION` with `Error: Temporal property Refines was violated`.

So a genuine refinement failure is reported as `SAFETY_VIOLATION` rather than
`REFINEMENT_VIOLATED`, and a caller branching on the token sees a safety violation with no
refinement in it.

This follows directly from `tla-94n`: 12 and 13 split on the shape of the formula, not on the
`.cfg` keyword. A refinement `PROPERTY` inherits whatever shapes the abstract `Spec` carries, and
a `[](P => []P)` conjunct in an abstract spec is ordinary rather than exotic.

Not fixed at source because it sat outside the `tla-94n` worker's footprint, which was right.

The fix needs care rather than a second `12)` arm: rc=12 from RUN A could be a refinement
violation or a genuine invariant violation in the concrete spec, and the exit code alone does not
separate them. RUN A declares no `INVARIANT` today, which may be enough to make the case
unambiguous. Check that before assuming it.

title: test-pipefail.sh cannot see workflow YAML, where the hazard was live
description:
`harness/test-pipefail.sh` bans `| grep -q`, `| grep -m` and `| head` across the tree, selecting
files by shebang rather than by extension so that files which do not exist yet are covered the
moment they land. GitHub workflow YAML has no shebang and no `.sh` suffix, so it is invisible to
the scanner.

That is not hypothetical. `.github/workflows/verify-puzzles.yml` carried three hits, one of them
the load-bearing toolchain-version assertion, and the workflow had been failing since 2026-08-06
without anyone seeing it. `tla-1qn` fixed the site. The gate that exists to catch this class
structurally could not see the file.

The argument for widening is that `run:` blocks in this repo set `set -euo pipefail` themselves,
so the hazard is live there in exactly the form the scanner was written for.

The `tla-1qn` worker measured the change and did not make it, correctly, since widening a gate's
selection is its own bead. What it costs: one entry in `SCAN_ROOTS` (currently `harness scripts
chapter`, `test-pipefail.sh:184`), a selector clause admitting `.github/workflows/*.yml`
(`:206-214`), and a `check_root .github 1` floor. It also confirmed the whole-line comment strip
at `:298` correctly swallows documentation that mentions the banned idiom, so the new
explanatory comment in the workflow will not self-trip the scanner.

title: §9.8's recognition stop asks about the problem, not the mechanism
description:
§9.8 tells a blind agent: "if you recognize this as a known published problem, say so immediately
and stop."

On the pilot one critic answered that question explicitly — "I do not recognize this as a known
published problem, it reads as a synthetic puzzle, so I proceeded" — and then, at the end,
identified the system as two-phase commit.

All three critics recognized 2PC. All three noticed while reading Rule 3, before opening the
spec. None stopped, and none was wrong not to. The problem IS synthetic and unpublished. The
control asks about provenance when the risk is mechanism.

§5.7 already screens mechanism rather than name, and the survey drawer says outright that name
novelty is not mechanism novelty. §9.8's stop condition never got the same treatment.

Fix: ask both, and treat them differently. Stop on a recognized published problem. Report a
recognized mechanism without stopping, because that is measurement rather than disqualification.
Asking it last leaks nothing, which the pilot confirmed on all three.

title: PUZZLE-SCREEN.md Q2 is calibrated for column A, so column C can never pass it
description:
Q2 asks whether the legal moves are given by the domain or decided by the learner. A critique
problem hands the learner an action set by construction, twice over: in the statement's rules and
again in the spec being critiqued. So a column-C problem answers Q2 "given" every time, which is
the puzzle answer, and it is structural rather than a wording defect.

Agent C hit this on the pilot and reported it instead of rewording around it. Its reading, which I
find persuasive: a column-C form of Q2 would ask whether the learner has to decide what a
REQUIREMENT is, which for the pilot is yes. The modeling judgment moves from "what are the
actions" to "which rules are state predicates, which are transition properties, and which the
observation vocabulary can carry at all".

The tally rule fires at three puzzle answers across Q2 to Q8, so one structural puzzle answer
doesn't sink a column-C problem today. It does mean the score is off by one for an entire column,
and Stage 5 authors eight of them.

notes:
WIDEN from Q2 to Q1 AND Q2. Agent D's independent screen (pilot step 5) found Q1 has the same defect: its system column reads 'the actions themselves', which column C can never claim for the same structural reason Q2 can't read 'decided'. A critique problem is handed an action set twice over.

Agent D also sharpened the diagnosis on Q2. It is not merely structurally given — the pilot's PROBLEM.md enumerates every action in prose as well, so delete the attached spec and the statement alone is still a complete action set. Doubly given, not structurally given.

The fix both readings point at is the same: the rubric needs a requirement-centric answer pair for Q1 and Q2, not a footnote on one row. For column C the question is whether the learner must decide what a REQUIREMENT is, which for the pilot is yes.

title: The two-sided answer check is both too loose and too strict
description:
The pilot's answer form checks a learner's conjunct twice: VIOLATED against the deficient spec
(rc=12), HOLDS against the reference (rc=0). Agent C measured both failure directions on the real
artifact.

**Too loose.** `Observe.issued => ("fire" \in Observe.approvedBy)` passes at 12 and 0 while saying
nothing about unanimity. Any single-department weakening does. The deficient spec's reachable set
exceeds the reference's by exactly 72 states, all `issued` with an approval set neither empty nor
full, so excluding any one of them satisfies the check. `PROBLEM.md` disqualifies the family in
prose ("hold for any Departments"), which is a human-graded line. A grader keyed on exit codes
alone admits it.

**Too strict.** The check pins rc=12, and an action-property violation exits 13 (bead tla-94n). So
any answer shaped `[][A]_vars` is rejected regardless of content. Agent C deliberately left the
statement vague about whether an action property is acceptable, because saying "an invariant"
would hint that transition properties are out, and that hint points straight at the ungradable
gap. So a critic can write a correct action property and score zero for its shape.

The loose direction needs a quantification requirement the checker can enforce rather than prose.
The strict direction needs tla-94n and tla-59s.

Found running the tla-kl5.11 pilot.

ANSWERED, at least for the atomicity-leakage direction, by the tla-x8s agent's proposal.

The third failure direction recorded in the earlier note is spec-dependence: a candidate passed against one correct spec and failed against a second whose step changed internal state without changing Observe. That agent rebuilt the case (a decide-then-commit lockbox) and ran a strict step obligation under both subscripts:

  coarse spec, [][A]_vars     -> OK rc=0
  fine spec,   [][A]_vars     -> LIVENESS_VIOLATION rc=13    <- reproduces this bead
  coarse spec, [][A]_Observe  -> OK rc=0
  fine spec,   [][A]_Observe  -> OK rc=0                     <- does not

Subscripting on Observe rather than vars excludes internal-only steps by construction: a step that moves internal state without moving the observation IS a stutter on Observe. So the atomicity half of this bead is closed by adopting the _Observe form, and any future two-state obligation must use it.

title: §6's pipeline has no repair loop when a gate comes back red
description:
§6's pipeline is eight steps and four gates with no arrow back. Step 2's gate reads "all green".
The pilot's step 2 came back PARTIAL, five of eleven adversarial variants uncaught, and the plan
says nothing about what happens next.

The gap isn't theoretical. §9.5 tells the verifier "do not fix anything; report only", which is
right, so the pipeline needs a named repair step and a re-verification, and it needs to say who
does each. Stage 5 authors 12 problems in a batch and this will come up every time.

Central resolved it for the pilot by dispatching a third agent to repair against the verifier's
findings and re-run the frozen variant set. That shape is worth keeping, because it holds the
separation: the verifier authors the variants adversarially, the variants freeze, and a repairer
who didn't author them has to make them go red. The test set doesn't move under the person trying
to pass it.

title: §5.2's grading engine can't grade a temporal obligation
description:
grade.sh generates `SPECIFICATION Spec / INVARIANT <op>(Observe)` for all three suites
(harness/grade.sh:356-357, mechanism table at :131-150). Obligations are `Req_*(o)` over one
observation record, variable-free by design so either spec can EXTEND the module. There's no
primed state and no pair of successive observations, so an obligation relating two states can't
be written at all.

That rules out a class of requirement, not an edge case. Any lifecycle system has rules shaped
"when X happens, Y must be cleared", and those are about transitions. Task shape B asks the
learner to write the property given a spec. §3.9 wants a violating trace with every property,
and a trace is a behaviour.

Concrete instance from the tla-kl5.11 pilot. The municipal-permit-review reference states rule 3
as `AmendmentClearsApprovals == [][ (amendments' # amendments) => (Observe'.approvedBy = {}) ]_vars`.
Agent A established it has no invariant form under the fixed `Observe`. A spec that amends
without clearing leaves stale "approved" entries, so `approvedBy` still reads full and every
invariant passes. Measured rc=13 with no invariant firing. Version-stamping would make it a
state fact, and it was rejected on separate grounds recorded in the reference's alternatives
note.

Two ways out, and I lean to the first:

1. Let `Req_*` take two records, emit a boxed action.
2. Keep it state-only and say so in §5.2.

Option 1 needs the exit-code row fixed first, because a violated action obligation exits 13 and
grade.sh reads 12 as UNMET. Option 2 is honest but narrows what a problem can ask a learner for.

The pilot isn't blocked. It proceeds with a state-expressible primary gap, which the unanimity
requirement supplies.

Files: harness/grade.sh, V2-PLAN.md
notes:
REFINEMENT from the pilot's step 2, and it matters for whoever picks this up: the amendment rule
has TWO independent blockers, and closing the one in the title does not close the other.

1. grade.sh is state-predicate-only. That's the title finding.
2. The fixed `Observe` exposes no amendment count, so an amendment is not observable at the graded
   interface at all.

Even with temporal obligations landed, rule 3 stays ungradable under this operator, because
`AmendmentClearsApprovals` reaches for the raw `amendments` variable rather than a field of
`Observe`. §3.3 says grading keys off Observe and never raw state, so as written that property
could not be a graded obligation regardless of the channel.

Agent B's v09 variant is the sharp instance. Freeze the amendment counter and the property goes
vacuous, since it's guarded by `amendments' # amendments`. Nothing in the graded interface can see
the difference.

Adding an `amendments` field to Observe is the obvious repair and central considered it during the
pilot, then left it. It's legitimate (a revision count is an observable fact about the permit
process, not a representation choice) but it buys no gate improvement until this bead lands,
because "an amendment increments the count" is still temporal. Recorded so the option isn't
re-derived from scratch.
close_reason:
Merged as 55c85fa (work commit b71ec34), plus af93ed2 for Gate.tla. Design captured in drawer_tla_puzzles_decisions_89795ff4c47c0358e2ea81e9.

A structureless spec — one variable, any permitted value at any time, no transitions, no causality — passed with zero witnesses against the shipped reference, and its operator was entirely honest, so this was never about lying. Root cause: every obligation was a single-state predicate, and no single-state predicate can constrain a transition relation. References may now state Step_*(o,p) obligations judged as a boxed action subscripted on Observe and declared PROPERTY. The _Observe subscript closes tla-nyrb's atomicity direction by construction. The frozen-operator trapdoor inside that fix is gated by a three-layer landmark check rather than a header note.

Four smaller defects landed with it: REPO_ROOT resolved from the caller's cwd so grading inside another repo ran that repo's verdict channel; rc=75/76/77 crashed the grader instead of grading the submission INVALID; the constants fragment went in unvalidated; and a selftest helper hardcoded one problem's directories. 58 assertions to 86.

Verified on main by central: the structureless spec now returns FAIL, under_constrained true, exit 1, with a real witness location. lint 0, test 0, 10 suites in 191.7s. Fourth site of the fragment-validator class filed separately.

title: §6's pilot pipeline never says who authors the seeded variants
description:
§9.5 tells the reference verifier to run each 'seeded-broken variant supplied' and confirm rc=12. Nothing upstream supplies them. §9.4 gives agent A three deliverables and variants aren't among them, and §5.5 describes the matrix without naming an author. Step 2 has a gate it can't run.

Whoever writes the variants must not be whoever wrote the invariant under test. The matrix asks whether a property ever says no, and an author who writes both tends to write variants their own invariant already catches. That's the self-verification trap the tla-kl5.2 wave was set up to break.

Resolved for the pilot by having agent B author the variants adversarially and then run the matrix, since agent A wrote the invariant. I think that pairing belongs in §6 and §9.5 rather than being re-decided per problem, because Stage 5 authors 12 problems in one batch and the decision won't survive being made twelve times.

Found running the tla-kl5.11 pilot.

Files: V2-PLAN.md

title: Gate the 'verdict.sh is the sole TLC entry point' invariant instead of remembering it
description:
The `tla-kl5.3` KG extraction (2026-08-07) declined to encode one relationship as a triple and
noted another was better expressed as a gate. Both are worth acting on.

**1. Make "verdict.sh is the sole TLC entry point" a GATE, not a fact to remember.**

Every harness component routes its TLC invocations through `harness/verdict.sh`, which holds the
canonical flags (`-workers 1`, `-noGenerateSpecTE`, `-metadir`) and the rc→token map:
`grade.sh`, `vacuity.sh`, `refinement.sh`, `seeded-bugs.sh`, and now `scripts/verify-puzzle.sh`.
The extractor verified it holds today — `grep -ln "java -" harness/*.sh` returns nothing.

**But nothing enforces it.** A future component that shells out to `java -cp ... tlc2.TLC`
directly would silently lose `-workers 1` (making counterexamples nondeterministic), lose the
corrected rc table, and re-introduce exactly the stdout-classification this project spent
`tla-syn` removing. That is a correctness invariant depending on human memory, which
gate-don't-advise says must not happen.

Add an assertion — `harness/test-pipefail.sh` already scans by shebang and walks the tree, so it
is the natural host, or a sibling check in `scripts/test`. Exempt `verdict.sh` itself. Note
`comment-gate.sh` and `screen.sh` are legitimately NOT in the set: they use "verdict" as a common
noun and never run TLC, so the assertion is about who launches TLC, not who says "verdict".

**2. `harness/grade.sh:407 token_for()` is a partial second copy of the rc→token map.**
Already filed as part of `tla-6nt`; noting the overlap so the two are not fixed twice. A single
source would make check 1 easier to state.

**3. Deliberately NOT encoded, and worth preserving as a judgement:** the extractor left the
SIGPIPE hazard and the rc=75/rc=14 findings out of the KG on the grounds that each is already
enforced by a gate (`test-pipefail.sh` scans unwritten files; the rc facts are fixture-asserted),
so a triple would duplicate a working enforcement. **If either gate is ever weakened, those facts
need somewhere else to live.** That is the trigger to revisit, not a reason to add them now.

Files: harness/test-pipefail.sh, scripts/test
acceptance_criteria: An assertion fails if any harness/scripts component launches TLC without going through verdict.sh; verdict.sh itself exempt.

Three consequences of `tla-i9m` that its worker correctly reported rather than editing out of
footprint, plus one methodology fix.

title: scripts/setup fails at the pip step — Debian PEP 668 externally-managed-environment
description:
`bash scripts/setup` completes its TLA+ toolchain half and then **fails at the pip step**:

    error: externally-managed-environment
    ... If you wish to install a non-Debian-packaged Python package, create a virtual
    environment using python3 -m venv ...
    setup: ERROR — pip install failed

This is Debian/Ubuntu PEP 668. `pip install -r docs-requirements.txt` into the system interpreter
is refused by design on this platform, so `scripts/setup` cannot succeed on a fresh box here.

Found 2026-08-07 running setup for real during tla-wl7. The jar install runs first and completed,
so the toolchain pin landed — but the script exits non-zero, which means anyone following the
documented setup path sees a failure, and `scripts/cibuild` phase ordering may inherit it.

OPTIONS, needs a decision rather than a default:
  (a) Create and use a project venv (`.venv/`), and have `server`/`deploy`/`cibuild` use its
      interpreter. Most correct, most moving parts, and it changes what `package_manager: pip`
      in the constitution means.
  (b) `pipx` for the mkdocs toolchain — it is an application, not a library, so pipx is arguably
      the right tool. Does not help if a plugin needs to be importable alongside.
  (c) `--break-system-packages`. Works, and is exactly what the constitution's `forbidden:` list
      exists to prohibit if anyone cares. Do not pick this silently.
  (d) Detect PEP 668 and degrade: skip the pip step with a clear message naming the fix, so the
      toolchain half still succeeds cleanly. Smallest change; leaves docs deps to the human.

CHECK FIRST whether the docs toolchain is even missing here — `mkdocs` may already be installed
system-wide, in which case the step is a no-op on this machine and the bug only bites a fresh
one. That changes the urgency but not the correctness.

Note this also affects `.claude/project-constitution.md`, which records `package_manager: pip`.
Whichever option wins, the constitution's rationale comment should say why.

Files: scripts/setup, .claude/project-constitution.md
acceptance_criteria: scripts/setup exits 0 on this machine and on a fresh Debian box; the chosen approach is recorded in the constitution's package_manager rationale.

title: gen-curriculum-map.sh hardcodes an absolute cd into the main checkout — worktree leak
description:
`scripts/gen-curriculum-map.sh:5` is:

    cd /home/frank/repos/tla-puzzles

An absolute path to the MAIN checkout. Run from any git worktree — which is where every
dispatched worker runs — it writes `CURRICULUM_MAP.md` into the main working tree instead of the
worktree. A silent cross-tree write, and exactly the leak `.claude/rules/dispatched-agents.md`
and loom's worker-isolation hooks exist to prevent. It is also why `tla-xme` could not fill the
`gen` verb in the constitution.

FIX (≤10 lines, single file, no new test — qualifies for the inline exception):

    cd "$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"

Resolve from the script's own location, never an absolute path.

Then fill `canonical_commands.gen: "bash scripts/gen-curriculum-map.sh"` in
`.claude/project-constitution.md` — the front-matter comment currently records the absolute `cd`
as the specific reason that verb is blank, so the comment needs updating in the same change.

The script's own header also points at `/tmp/gen-curriculum-map.sh`, a stale path from when it
lived in /tmp; worth correcting while there.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS: a worker told to run the project's generator would silently
corrupt the main checkout's working tree mid-wave, and the damage would surface as unexplained
dirty state in an unrelated bead.

title: SIGPIPE-under-pipefail makes harness structural assertions silently report present patterns as absent
description:
`harness/test-verdict.sh:90` uses:

    if verdict_code | grep -qE -- "$pattern"; then

Under `set -o pipefail`, `grep -q` exits the instant it matches, the producer on the left gets
SIGPIPE, and the pipeline returns **141**. Inside an `if`, 141 is simply falsy and `set -e` does
not fire — so the assertion reports the pattern ABSENT when it is PRESENT. A false FAIL, not a
false PASS, which is the survivable direction but still a test that lies.

REPRODUCED 2026-08-06, and the trigger is NOT what it first looks like:

    big() { local i; for ((i=0;i<$1;i++)); do echo "MATCHME line $i padding"; done; }
    big 10    | grep -qE MATCHME   -> rc=0
    big 1000  | grep -qE MATCHME   -> rc=141
    big 50000 | grep -qE MATCHME   -> rc=141

What matters is **how much the PRODUCER writes**, not how big any file is. The originally
suspected shape — `sed <large-file> | grep -q` — does NOT reproduce it: tested against a 20 KB
script and a 200,000-line stream, both rc=0 or a genuine rc=1. So the hazard is specifically a
SHELL FUNCTION (or any slow/chatty producer) piped into an early-exiting consumer.

WHY IT PASSES TODAY: `verdict_code` emits a single token, far under the pipe buffer, so grep
consumes everything before exiting and no SIGPIPE occurs. The test is correct by accident of
output size. It starts lying the moment that function becomes chatty — adds a debug line, echoes
the command it ran, anything.

FIX: capture first, match second, so no pipe is live when grep exits.

    out=$(verdict_code) || true
    if printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -qE -- "$pattern"; then

Or drop `pipefail` for the assertion, or use `grep -c` and compare. Capture-then-match is
preferred — it also makes the captured output available for the failure message, which the
current shape throws away.

SWEEP THE WHOLE HARNESS, not just this line: `harness/comment-gate.sh`, `harness/screen.sh`,
`harness/vacuity.sh` and their suites all use structural assertions of this family, and
`tla-kl5.5`/`tla-kl5.7` are landing more of them as this is filed. Grep for `| *grep -q` under a
`pipefail` shell and fix each site.

GATE IT: add a regression test that pins the fix — a deliberately chatty producer piped into an
early-exiting matcher, asserting the assertion still reports PRESENT. Without that, this returns
the moment someone reintroduces the idiom, and it returns silently.

Files: harness/test-verdict.sh, harness/test-vacuity.sh, harness/comment-gate.sh, harness/screen.sh

Acceptance: no `| grep -q` under pipefail survives in harness/; a regression test with a chatty
producer pins the fix; all harness suites still green.
acceptance_criteria: No '| grep -q' under pipefail survives in harness/; a regression test with a chatty producer pins the fix; all harness suites green.
notes: INDEPENDENTLY CORROBORATED by tla-kl5.5, which hit the same thing in its own suite: 'grep -q in a pipeline under set -o pipefail reports a present pattern as absent'. It attributed the trigger to sed-over-a-file, and central's controlled reproduction could NOT make sed do it (20KB file and a 200,000-line stream both gave rc=0 or a genuine rc=1) while a shell-function producer reproduced at 1000 lines and above. Two workers hitting it with different producers suggests the trigger is TIMING, not a size threshold — whether the consumer exits before the producer finishes flushing. That is worse than a deterministic bug: it makes the false FAIL intermittent, so a suite can be green on one run and red on the next with no code change. Prefer capture-then-match everywhere over trying to characterize the threshold.
close_reason: Swept 24 early-exiting sites across 10 files; merged to main, rules recorded in commit f4b8e69. Seven suites green at 255 assertions (21+25+71+26+57+43+12). THE FIX IN THE BEAD AND IN MY BRIEF WAS WRONG and the worker measured it: capture-then-match with printf still returns 141, because the printf builtin forks into the pipeline and takes SIGPIPE exactly as a shell function does — the live pipe is the bug, not the producer. Here-strings are the actual fix, rc=0 at 21 MB. Central independently reproduced all three shapes and relayed the correction to two workers still running under the bad advice. Three of the 24 sites were GUARDS rather than assertions, including the SYMMETRY/VIEW soundness check in refinement.sh where a 141 lets an unsound temporal reduction through unflagged — a false PASS on a correctness gate, not the false FAIL the bead described. No assertion changed behaviour: every producer in the tree is currently small enough that the consumer never won the race, confirming the correct-by-accident thesis at all 24 sites rather than just the one. New gate harness/test-pipefail.sh bans the shape tree-wide by shebang and scans the tree, so files not yet written are covered; central verified it exits 1 on a planted violation with exact file:line and 0 when clean.

title: Write .claude/rules/dispatched-agents.md — the pre-flight battery loom's conventions assume exists
description:
Loom's shipped conventions (.claude/rules/loom-conventions.md) say: "Your project's
`.claude/rules/dispatched-agents.md` carries the battery itself and the project-specific
hazards. Read it before any dispatch." That file DOES NOT EXIST in this project — the only
file in .claude/rules/ is loom-conventions.md itself.

The 2026-08-06 harness wave (tla-kl5.4/.9/.10) worked around it by inlining the whole
pre-flight battery into each of the three briefs by hand. That is three copies of the same
text, drifting from the moment they were written, and the next dispatcher has to remember to
write it a fourth time.

CONTENT THE FILE MUST CARRY, all of it learned the hard way in that wave:

1. REPO-IDENTITY CHECK. `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`, then confirm V2-PLAN.md and
   QUALITY_GATE.md exist at that root. A wrong-repo worktree resolves relative paths to THAT
   repo's real files of the same name, so obeying the brief is what does the damage. A worker
   that finds a mismatch ABORTS and reports; it never adapts.
2. RELATIVE PATHS ONLY. isolation:"worktree" sets cwd; it does NOT sandbox the filesystem, so
   Edit/Write accept any absolute path and an absolute path leaks into the shared checkout.
3. THE BEADS COMMIT HAZARD, specific to this repo. .git/hooks/pre-commit runs
   `bd hooks run pre-commit`, which re-exports .beads/issues.jsonl. In a parallel wave every
   worker's commit would then carry that file and collide with every sibling. Workers commit
   with `git commit --no-verify` and `git add <explicit paths>` — NEVER `git add -A`. Beads
   state is owned centrally by the dispatcher.
4. CONSTITUTION READ AS STEP 0. canonical_commands is DELIBERATELY EMPTY here — scripts/test is
   an unwired `exit 2` stub, so a worker that "runs the project's tests" gets a meaningless
   failure. Say so explicitly or every worker rediscovers it.
5. TOOLCHAIN PIN. `tlc 2>&1 | head -1` must report TLC2 Version 2026.03.04.183147 — the version
   every constant in V2-PLAN.md §5 was verified against. pcal is at ~/.nix-profile/bin/pcal.
6. FOOTPRINT VERIFICATION ON THE WAY OUT. `git diff --stat main HEAD`, never a
   `git -C <main-path>` redirect (the isolation harness refuses it). Compare against the bead's
   declared Files: line and report any deviation.
7. CLAIM PROVENANCE. Every load-bearing claim carries EITHER a citation — the command run and
   its result, or a file:line — OR the literal marker INFERRED. Never neither. A citation is a
   pointer, not a rationale.

Files: .claude/rules/dispatched-agents.md

Acceptance: the file exists and carries all seven items; a future dispatch brief can cite it
instead of inlining the battery.
acceptance_criteria: The file exists and carries all seven items; a dispatch brief can cite it instead of inlining the battery.
close_reason: Wrote .claude/rules/dispatched-agents.md in commit d85b0cb as a FORK of loom's canonical copy, following the liza_base pattern (canonical stays in loom; forks carry local hazards). Prior art found via the bd-claim-research hook before designing: loom/.claude/rules/dispatched-agents.md (979 lines) and liza_base's 507-line fork already existed, so this adapts rather than invents. Two corrections to what the v2 harness wave had hand-copied into three briefs: (1) repo identity is 'git remote -v' per loom-stdi, not a file-existence check; (2) the battery MUST be separate Bash calls because the worktree-isolation harness statically refuses command substitution and brace grouping, so a worker handed one pasteable block improvises a split nobody reviewed. Also carries five tla-puzzles-specific hazards loom does not have: the beads pre-commit hook that makes 'git commit --no-verify' REQUIRED here (an inversion of liza_base's prohibition), canonical_commands deliberately empty because the 8 scripts/ stubs are exit 2 (tla-xme), the TLC 2026.03.04.183147 version pin that every V2-PLAN.md section-5 constant depends on, the centrally-owned shared files harness/Gate.tla and harness/verdict.sh, and puzzles/ being v1 and read-only for v2 work. Step 2 detects a missing isolation:'worktree' by path shape rather than pwd==toplevel, which cannot see it because in the main tree those are equal — wording taken from the liza_base 2026-06-21 finding where exactly that slipped through.

title: Stage 4 §6b.4 — attempt + impasse logging: this is the research artifact
description:
Goal: THERE IS NO PUBLISHED RECORD OF TLA+ LEARNER ERRORS ANYWHERE — no misconception catalogue,
no corpus, no controlled study. A tutor directory that logs attempts, impasses, what unlocked
each one, and how many edits preceded a pass produces exactly the artifact the field lacks, for a
language where nobody has it. That makes the logging a DELIVERABLE, not instrumentation.

Log per attempt: timestamp · problem id · spec submitted · verdict object · questions asked ·
prompts given · whether the unlock was STRATEGIC or SPECIFIC.

ALSO LOG THE IMPASSE KIND — load-bearing, not nice-to-have. Every problem sits in a domain Frank
does not know (§2.2), so an impasse is either:

  DOMAIN   — "I don't understand the rules of the system"       → the statement is BROKEN; fix it
  MODELING — "I understand it, I don't know how to represent it" → the problem is HARD; leave it

These look IDENTICAL from outside, and §7.1's progressive refinement policy cannot be applied
without the distinction: a blind-solve round where all three fail reads as "underspecified", and
you would go rewrite a statement that was fine. The tutor ASKS DIRECTLY at every impasse — "is it
the rules of the system that are unclear, or how to model them?" — and records the answer.
DO NOT INFER IT.

Files: (tla-practice/ log schema — outside this repo)
acceptance_criteria: Schema covers all seven per-attempt fields plus impasse kind; the tutor ASKS rather than infers; a worked example log exists from the pilot.

title: Stage 5 §7 — author batch 1: the 12 diagonal cells of the §2.1 grid
description:
AUTOFAN-EXCLUDE: attended — the between-batch barrier is a human working the problems. Decompose
into per-problem children when the grid cells are picked; do not auto-dispatch this bead.

Goal: BATCH 1 = THE DIAGONAL of the §2.1 grid, ~12 problems. Walking the diagonal maximizes
situation × task-shape variety in the smallest possible set, so the first telemetry is broad
rather than deep. Batch 1 is PlusCal (§3b step 2).

BATCHED, NOT ONE BIG FAN-OUT (§7.0). An earlier draft said to pipeline all problems with no
barriers, for throughput. That was SUPERSEDED 2026-08-06 and must not be "fixed" back. The
batching is PEDAGOGICAL, not operational: Frank works each batch before the next is authored, so
real learner telemetry informs the remaining problems — batch 1's data then shapes ~48 problems
instead of 0. Within a batch, pipeline freely; the barrier is BETWEEN batches, at the point where
a human works them.

Budget ~8 agent invocations per problem (1 author + 1 verifier + 1 statement + 1 leakage + 3
solvers + 1 commenter). 12 problems ≈ 96 invocations. At 60 problems it is ~480. This is the
intended scale, not an overrun.

Every problem runs the full §6 pipeline and BOTH screens (§5.7, §5.7b — §5.7b at statement time,
since the same domain yields a puzzle or a system depending on wording). Every property ships
with one satisfying AND one violating trace (§3.9 — multiple positive instances had no measured
effect; negative instances did).

PROGRESSIVE REFINEMENT POLICY between batches (§7.1) — the line that keeps this honest:
  REFINE PROBLEMS THAT ARE BROKEN, NOT PROBLEMS THAT ARE HARD.
  Fix: ambiguous statement · misfiring harness · a mechanism that turns out to be burned · a
       problem whose blind-solve spread was wrong.
  Leave alone: frustrating but well-formed.
Two reasons it matters: (1) Frank is simultaneously the subject and the instrument, and you
cannot measure progress with a ruler you are bending; (2) 78% of Kornell & Bjork's participants
preferred the format that taught them worst, so his in-the-moment sense that a problem is BAD is
unreliable for difficulty — though RELIABLE for ambiguity. Treat "this was confusing" as a bug
report and "this was hard" as a non-event.

CALIBRATION (§7.5): difficulty tracks NESTING DEPTH, not size — nested quantifiers ~34% success
vs ~53% unnested; anything temporal ~27%, so budget ~2× attempts there. Learners quit around
attempt 6 (32.6% gave up after a mean of 5.85 edits). Target 20-40 minutes; if the blind solvers
take materially longer, the problem is too big.

FORMAT TECHNIQUES WORTH USING (§7.4): ENSEEIHT's split — withhold practice solutions, publish
fully-worked EXAM solutions, which is also where post-hoc commentary belongs. Bordeaux's
"most permissive" framing — ask for the MOST PERMISSIVE correct design, not A correct one; no
memorizable canonical answer, and "does A admit behaviours B rejects, both still correct?" is
mechanically checkable.

Files: (tla-practice/ + tla-answers/ — outside this repo)
acceptance_criteria: 12 problems on the diagonal, each through all 8 pipeline steps and both screens; batch-1 telemetry captured before batch 2 is authored.
notes:
SUPERSEDED IN PART, 2026-08-07. Batch 1 is no longer the ~12-cell diagonal for the first delivery. Frank agreed to a smaller first set, and two red-team passes then inverted it further: ONE problem, delivered through a real practice/answers boundary, gating the rest on his first attempt.

The diagonal's REASON survives and this bead should keep it. §2.1 makes the diagonal the checkable form of §3.4 (never two consecutive problems sharing a situation or a task shape, d=0.83). The revised first set must still be 4-6 CELLS across shapes and situations, not 4-6 of one column — central's original all-column-A proposal violated §3.4 and did not notice.

Current plan: drawer_tla_puzzles_decisions_89795ff4c47c0358e2ea81e9 (revised).

title: Stage 4 §6b.3 — the tutor is a LANGUAGE tutor, not a solution tutor
description:
Goal: a tutor that runs in tla-practice/ and GENUINELY DOES NOT POSSESS the answer — not "is
instructed not to peek", DOES NOT HAVE IT. It knows TLA+/PlusCal and learntla content. It
DECLINES "is my approach right?", because that is the thing being measured.

This constraint is not merely safe, it is the EVIDENCE-BACKED INTERVENTION (§6b.3). Perkins &
Martin (ERIC ED295618): content-free strategic prompts ALONE resolved 32% (conservative) to 55%
(liberal) of impasses; specific hints added only ~15-17% on top — "if the knowledge is there to
be marshalled, strategic questions usually suffice." An agent that structurally cannot give the
answer is forced into the intervention that works best anyway.

DIAGNOSTIC BONUS: when a strategic prompt unlocks Frank, the knowledge was INERT, not ABSENT — a
different problem with a different remedy, and one you can only distinguish by prompting BEFORE
hinting.

Warm but NOT reassuring-by-default (§9.11). The learner will systematically prefer the interaction
style that teaches worst — 78% of Kornell & Bjork's participants preferred the format that taught
them worst — so do not optimize for in-the-moment comfort.

Require the predict → model → check → explain-the-divergence loop (§7.4). A prediction commitment
BEFORE running TLC is the defense against grader-gaming; students otherwise "learn the grader,
not the concepts." The self-explanation prompt is the piece with meta-analytic support (g=0.55).

Briefs: V2-PLAN.md §9.11 (system prompt) and §9.10 (directory builder).

Files: (tla-practice/.claude/ — outside this repo)
acceptance_criteria: Tutor answers language questions, declines approach questions, and asks for a prediction before any TLC run.

title: Stage 4 §6b.2 — grader returns a verdict object, never a diff
description:
Goal: the grader is a SEPARATE invocation with read access to tla-answers/. It takes
(learner spec, problem id) and returns a VERDICT OBJECT: pass/fail per obligation plus ERROR
LOCATION (§3.7). Never reference conjuncts, never a diff — that leaks the decomposition (§6b.2).

Wraps harness/grade.sh. The isolation boundary is the entire point: the tutor can invoke this and
cannot see its inputs. If the tutor and the grader ever share a filesystem view, the design has
failed regardless of what the prompts say (§6b.1).

Files: (tla-practice/ client + tla-answers/ grader — outside this repo)

RED: GIVEN a wrong learner spec, WHEN the grader returns, THEN the verdict object contains an
error location and contains NO substring of any reference conjunct.
acceptance_criteria: Verdict-object schema fixed; leak test passing; the tutor has no read path to the grader's inputs.

title: Stage 4 §6b.1-2 — scaffold tla-practice/ + tla-answers/ with STRUCTURAL isolation
description:
Goal: Frank works the problems through a live Claude configuration rather than reading static
text — it presents the problem, answers questions, and drives review. He raised the leakage risk
himself, and it is the whole design constraint.

INSTRUCTION ISOLATION IS NOT ISOLATION (§6b.1). Telling an agent not to look at the answers DOES
NOT WORK — an agent debugging a harness failure will `cat` the reference, and it will be right to.
Isolation must be structural.

  Leak vector                                              Fix
  filesystem — reference readable from the working tree    two directories, not one
  context bleed — one agent both answers and holds it      two agents, different filesystem views
  git history — reference ever committed alongside         separate repo, never co-committed
  grader output — "missing conjunct 3 of the reference"    return a verdict object, never a diff
  TRAINING DATA — the model already knows burned problems  UNCLOSABLE. This is the operational
                                                           reason §5.7 screening is not optional.

ARCHITECTURE (§6b.2):
  tla-practice/ — statements, Frank's attempts, the harness CLIENT, its own .claude/. This is
                  where Frank and the tutor live.
  tla-answers/  — references, seeded variants, expected state counts, post-hoc commentary.
                  SEPARATE REPO, not co-located, denied in tla-practice/.claude/settings.json.

Files: (new repos ~/repos/tla-practice and ~/repos/tla-answers — outside this repo)

RED: INVARIANT: from inside tla-practice/, no path under tla-answers/ is readable — verified by an
actual attempted read, never by reading the settings file and believing it.
acceptance_criteria: Both repos exist; the deny rule is present AND demonstrated by a failed read attempt; no commit ever contains files from both.

title: Stage 2 §5.7 + §5.7b — the two independent screens: mechanism collision, and puzzle-versus-system
description:
Goal: two INDEPENDENT screens over every candidate problem. A candidate can pass one cleanly and
still be useless, which is why they are two screens and not one.

§5.7 MECHANISM COLLISION — "has someone already solved this?"
  gh api -X GET search/code -f q='<SystemName> language:tla' --jq '.total_count'
  Treat >3 hits as BURNED. Then the step that catches the misses: GREP THE MECHANISM, NOT THE
  NAME, against the tlaplus/Examples README table. "Warehouse robot coordination" is
  MisraReachability + mutual exclusion; "seat reservation" is the allocator; "leader failover"
  is Paxos. NAME NOVELTY IS NOT MECHANISM NOVELTY.

§5.7b PUZZLE-VERSUS-SYSTEM — "is it even the right KIND of thing?"
  THE SCREEN: if you hand the learner the legal moves, is there anything left to model? If no,
  it is a puzzle. Cut it, or add agents and failure until it isn't.

               | Puzzle                  | System
  legal moves  | given by the domain     | the thing you have to decide
  the question | is the goal reachable?  | is this design correct?
  who works    | TLC searches            | you model, TLC checks
  difficulty   | state-space size        | abstraction choice

  Why this is not pedantry: every puzzle in tlaplus/Examples — Die Hard, Tower of Hanoi,
  N-Queens, missionaries and cannibals, the sliding block puzzle — is flagged BEGINNER. Not
  because they are small, but because the modeling was pre-done by whoever wrote the rules. And
  "puzzles where the state space is handed to you and the work is search" is the FIRST of the
  four categories the corpus survey found the entire public corpus consists of. It is the
  category this project is defined against.

  LOCAL REPRESENTATION CHOICES DO NOT RESCUE A PUZZLE. A puzzle usually still offers real
  choices — change-ringing offers bells→positions vs positions→bells (inverse functions; picking
  wrong makes half the constraints awkward), and explicit visited-row history vs noticing that a
  repeated row IS a repeated state so TLC's own dedup enforces no-repeats for free. Genuine and
  interesting, but LOCAL — about transcribing a given action set tidily, not deciding what the
  actions are. Good taste, not modeling judgment, and only the second is what we teach.

  RESCUE PATTERN: add agents and fallibility, converting search into specification.

  TEETH: restaurant seating FAILS as "seat this party optimally" (bin-packing) and PASSES as
  "model the host stand with walk-ins and reservations arriving concurrently". Same domain,
  different statement — THE SCREEN IS WHAT TELLS YOU WHICH FRAMING YOU WROTE. So it runs at
  STATEMENT time (§6 step 4) as well as at domain-selection time; passing once does not
  immunize a domain.

§5.7 is mechanizable. §5.7b is a JUDGMENT RUBRIC — ship it as a checklist that the statement
author and the leakage checker both run, not as a script pretending to decide it.

Feed in the §2.2 pre-screen suspicions so the screen is not run blind (restaurant seating →
bin-packing; library holds / community garden / airline standby → the Resource Allocator in
different dress; orchestra auditions → tournament ranking, so at most one of the two survives;
change-ringing → fails §5.7b, rescuable but not in batch one; beekeeping → possibly too fuzzy
to state crisply enough for §3.2).

Independent of the verdict channel — no TLC involved — so it can start immediately.

Files: harness/screen.sh, harness/PUZZLE-SCREEN.md

RED: GIVEN "restaurant seating: seat this party optimally", WHEN the §5.7b rubric is applied,
THEN it is rejected as a puzzle; and GIVEN "model the host stand with walk-ins and reservations
arriving concurrently", THEN the same rubric accepts it as a system.
acceptance_criteria: screen.sh reports burned/clear by name AND mechanism; PUZZLE-SCREEN.md carries the rubric with the restaurant-seating pair as its worked example; both cited from the §9.6 statement-author brief.
close_reason: harness/screen.sh (§5.7) + PUZZLE-SCREEN.md (§5.7b rubric); 71 assertions green on merged main. §9.6/§9.7 briefs now cite both.

title: Stage 2 §5.6 — comment-pass gate (the naive stripper deletes the spec)
description:
Goal: enforce §3.8 — comments are added in a SEPARATE post-freeze pass, because comments written
alongside a spec bend the spec toward the commentary. The gate: strip comments from the frozen
and the commented versions, diff, require identical.

WRINKLE THAT BREAKS THE NAIVE IMPLEMENTATION: in PlusCal specs the algorithm lives inside
`(* --algorithm ... *)`. A naive comment stripper DELETES THE SPEC and the gate then compares two
empty files and passes. The stripper must preserve the block containing --algorithm /
--fair algorithm, and the \* BEGIN/END TRANSLATION markers.

CLEANER GATE FOR PLUSCAL: re-run pcal after commenting and require the TRANSLATION block to be
BYTE-IDENTICAL. Comments inside the algorithm block are not carried into the generated TLA+, so
any change at all means the pass touched the algorithm. Prefer this where the spec is PlusCal.

Independent of the verdict channel — this is text processing, not TLC — so it can start
immediately, in parallel with §5.1.

Files: harness/comment-gate.sh

RED: GIVEN a PlusCal spec whose algorithm lives inside (* --algorithm ... *), WHEN comment-gate.sh
strips comments, THEN the algorithm block survives and the gate compares real specs — a naive
stripper that deletes it must FAIL this test.
acceptance_criteria: PlusCal algorithm block preserved; BEGIN/END TRANSLATION markers preserved; pcal re-run path implemented; a commented-and-also-edited spec is rejected.
close_reason: harness/comment-gate.sh, two required checks (strip-and-diff + pcal re-translation); 25 assertions green on merged main. RED reproducible via COMMENT_GATE_STRIPPER=naive.

title: Stage 2 §5.5 — seeded-bug matrix: the only mechanical defense against Inv == TRUE
description:
Goal: state "this spec catches this bug" mechanically — rc==12 against the variant AND rc==0
against the reference. This is the ONLY mechanical defense against a learner writing
`Inv == TRUE`, which otherwise passes every check that asks "does your property hold".

CAVEAT TO RECORD IN THE CODE, not just here: only ~10.9% of real faulty student specs are one
mutation away from correct — real mistakes are multi-step — and 39.3% of single mutations are
semantically INERT. Mutants of our own reference are systematically unlike real learner errors.
This is a BOOTSTRAP, not a proxy for learner behaviour. The comment belongs in seeded-bugs.sh so
the next reader cannot mistake it for a validated instrument.

Diff counterexamples via ALIAS + -dumpTrace json: normalize state BEFORE dumping, and diff the
ACTION-NAME SEQUENCE PLUS TRACE LENGTH, which are stable. Concrete values vary with the learner's
representation and must NOT be diffed — diffing them would penalize exactly the representational
freedom §3.2 exists to protect.

Files: harness/seeded-bugs.sh

RED: GIVEN a reference spec, a seeded variant, and a learner property, WHEN seeded-bugs.sh runs,
THEN it passes only on rc==0-against-reference AND rc==12-against-variant — and `Inv == TRUE`
fails the matrix.
acceptance_criteria: Matrix runner working; Inv==TRUE rejected; trace diffing compares action-name sequence + length only; the 10.9%/39.3% caveat is a comment in the file.
notes: FILES LINE CORRECTED at close: the bead declared only harness/seeded-bugs.sh, but the work legitimately spans harness/seeded-bugs.sh AND harness/fixtures/seeded-bugs/. The dispatch brief granted both; the bead line did not. An under-declared Files: line makes the fan-out detector treat the footprint as smaller than it is, which is the direction that causes collisions rather than missed parallelism. Actual footprint: harness/seeded-bugs.sh, harness/fixtures/seeded-bugs/.
close_reason: harness/seeded-bugs.sh + 22 files, merged to main; rules hazard recorded in 95fcdf1. 37 assertions green, and all eight suites green together at 292 (21+25+71+26+57+43+12+37). STAGE 2 IS COMPLETE — tla-kl5.11, the pilot, is unblocked. Central verified the three load-bearing behaviours directly: a good property returns BUGS_CAUGHT, Inv == TRUE returns PROPERTY_TOO_WEAK (the bead's RED), and an inert variant set returns VARIANT_INERT for a GOOD and a BAD property ALIKE — which is the attribution property that keeps a defect in our own variant set off the learner's bill. The phase ordering is what carries that: the instrument is checked before the submission, and mutation M3 shows that removing the inert check makes AlwaysTrue come back PROPERTY_TOO_WEAK, the right exit code attributed to the wrong party. Ten mutations all turn the suite red, including M5, which proves the trace comparator does not diff concrete values — diffing them would report two identical behaviours in different representations as divergent, the exact section 3.2 penalty this project forbids. Worker also independently confirmed the here-string SIGPIPE correction and converted five live pipes in its own selftest; harness/test-pipefail.sh now scans 15 shell files including both of its new ones.

title: CI downloads tla2tools.jar from 'latest' — pin the TLC release
description:
.github/workflows/verify-puzzles.yml downloads:

  https://github.com/tlaplus/tlaplus/releases/latest/download/tla2tools.jar

`latest` means a new TLC release silently changes verification behavior with no commit to this repo. For a project whose whole premise is mechanically verified specs, the checker version is part of the contract and must be pinned.

Fix: pin the release tag, and ideally checksum the jar.

Good news that makes pinning cheap rather than restrictive: TLC's state counts for a completed exhaustive run are extremely stable. Measured identical (883 generated / 343 distinct / depth 19) across workers 1/4/8, three fingerprint polynomials, and THREE TLC releases spanning roughly seven years (2.15, 2.19, 2026.03.04). Symmetry-reduced runs were likewise identical (21/10) across all three versions. So pinning costs nothing in practice and buys reproducibility.

Note for any future Apalache track: Apalache 0.60.0 reportedly requires Java 25, while this workflow runs Java 21 — a second JDK would be needed.
acceptance_criteria: The workflow pins a specific tla2tools release tag (ideally checksummed) instead of tracking latest.
notes:
INVESTIGATED 2026-08-06 — THE PROBLEM IS BIGGER THAN 'PIN THE RELEASE'. Three different TLCs are in play and no two agree.

  CI today:  https://.../releases/latest/download/tla2tools.jar  ->  v1.7.4, published 2024-08-05.
             'latest' skips v1.8.0 because v1.8.0 is flagged PRERELEASE (verified: gh api
             repos/tlaplus/tlaplus/releases/latest -> v1.7.4). So CI has been running a 2024
             build this whole time.
  Local:     ~/lib/tla2tools.jar, TLC2 Version 2026.03.04.183147 (rev 52c0195), file dated Mar 5.
             This matches NO tagged release — it is a nightly/dev build. There is no 'nightly'
             release tag either (gh api .../releases/tags/nightly -> 404).
  Newest:    v1.8.0 'The Clarke release', prerelease=true, published 2026-07-31, TLC2 Version
             2026.07.31.184830.

CONSEQUENCE, and this is the real finding: EVERY empirical constant in V2-PLAN.md section 5 — the
exit-code table, the frozen-mapping probe, the total==0 dead-action predicate, the 0-initial-states
gate behavior — was verified against a build that CANNOT BE OBTAINED FROM ANY RELEASE URL. The
plan says 'do re-verify if you change TLC versions'; it did not anticipate that the verified
version is unreachable, so the constants are currently unreproducible by anyone but this machine.

MITIGATING EVIDENCE: the tla-kl5.3 survey independently re-ran the rc table and the frozen-mapping
probe on 2026.07.31.184830 (v1.8.0) and reported both holding. So v1.8.0 is corroborated for the
constants that matter most, by a run that was not looking for that result.

NOT JUST A CI FIX ANYMORE: pinning CI without moving local leaves two versions; moving local
without re-verifying leaves the constants asserted against a build nobody runs. Needs a decision
on which version is canonical for the project, then a re-verification pass against it.
close_reason: CI pinned to v1.8.0 in commit 43b4d2e, and the smoke check now ASSERTS the version string rather than logging it behind || true — a pin nobody checks is precisely how this drifted unnoticed. Investigation found the problem was larger than the bead assumed: releases/latest/download/ resolved to v1.7.4 (2024-08-05) because GitHub's 'latest' skips prereleases and v1.8.0 is flagged as one, so CI had been running a 2024 build while every empirical constant in V2-PLAN.md section 5 was verified against a 2026 nightly that matches no tagged release at all. Frank chose v1.8.0 'The Clarke release' (TLC2 2026.07.31.184830) as canonical. title: verify-puzzle.sh should classify by TLC exit code, not stdout greps; and must pin -workers 1
description:
scripts/verify-puzzle.sh classifies TLC results by grepping stdout. TLC has a clean, stable exit-code channel that makes every one of those greps unnecessary and immune to message-wording drift across releases.

Measured on TLC 2026.03.04 / tla2tools 1.8.0:
  0   success ("No error has been found")
  10  ASSUME or -postCondition evaluated FALSE
  11  deadlock
  12  safety violation (INVARIANT)
  13  liveness / action-property violation (PROPERTY, incl. refinement)
  150 parse or semantic failure
  151 config failure
  255 file not found

Switching to $? is faster, more precise (13 vs 12 distinguishes a property from an invariant violation, which grep cannot), and does not break when TLC rewords a message.

RELATED HAZARD, same file: the script does not pass -workers. It gets 1 by default today, but counterexample traces are NOT deterministic above one worker — measured, same spec and version, five runs at -workers 8 produced three different traces (trace LENGTH was stable at 4, the path was not). Any check that diffs a counterexample must pin -workers 1 explicitly rather than rely on the default.

Recommended invocation shape:
  tlc -workers 1 -deadlock -noGenerateSpecTE -nowarning \
      -coverage 1 -dumpTrace json trace.json \
      -metadir "$SCRATCH/states" Harness.tla -config Harness.cfg
(-metadir keeps states/ out of the tree; -noGenerateSpecTE stops the *_TTrace_*.tla litter already accumulating in puzzles/T01-the-light-switch/solution/.)
acceptance_criteria: verify-puzzle.sh branches on $? rather than grepping TLC stdout, and passes -workers 1 explicitly.
notes: Now depends on tla-kl5.4 (harness §5.1 verdict channel), which owns the canonical rc table and the -workers 1 constraint. Rewire verify-puzzle.sh to consume harness/verdict.sh rather than reimplementing the table — §5.1 says 'replace stdout greps with exit codes THROUGHOUT', and this bead is the v1-facing half of that.
close_reason: Rewired in commit 1dcb164, merged to main at 66cba9c. verify-puzzle.sh no longer runs TLC at all — it delegates to harness/verdict.sh and maps that one table onto v1's verdict vocabulary, so -workers 1 is pinned by INHERITANCE rather than repetition, with a structural assertion gating that no direct TLC call returns. Suite grew 2 to 33 assertions; full 107-dir corpus sweep byte-identical pre and post (115 lines, diff clean). Both banned-idiom sites DELETED outright, closing half of tla-4u0. THE GREPS WERE NOT MERELY INELEGANT — they produced two outright FALSE PASSES: rc=10 (failing ASSUME) and rc=151 (cfg naming an undefined operator) both reported PASS-OTHER at exit 0. And the headline finding, central-verified: V2-PLAN.md section 5.1's rc table was SIX CODES SHORT (14, 75, 76, 77, 152, 153), read straight from the pinned jar's own enum via javap on tlc2.output.EC$ExitStatus. rc=75 FAILURE_SPEC_EVAL is LIVE on the corpus — puzzles/T29-unchanged/solution/Clock_buggy.tla exits 75 with 'Successor state is not completely specified by action Tick', which central reproduced. The old chain classified it PASS-VIOLATION only because it matched the Trace exploration line of the *_TTrace_*.tla file TLC emits alongside the error — and the canonical invocation suppresses that file with -noGenerateSpecTE, so adopting the canonical invocation while keeping the greps would have silently deleted the only thing the verdict rested on. That is this bead's thesis demonstrated on live data.

title: Research: art-of-memory / connected-discourse loci → concrete spec-as-narrative encoding guidance
description:
Design-cycle research spawn (C4) for the 'pangram-set + spaced-recall TLA+ mastery method' design cycle (design-doc drawer_tla_puzzles_decisions_8af15aed4e3d4a625f8d5ec5; grounded in exploration drawer_tla_puzzles_decisions_781911016d78a8fc67d62269, finding F10).

QUESTION: The exploration's first deep-research round leaned on the EXPERIMENTAL psychology of method-of-loci (word-list paradigm), under-weighting loci's PARADIGMATIC home — memorizing connected, coherent DISCOURSE (orators' speeches). Does the classical art-of-memory literature (Yates 1966 'The Art of Memory'; Rhetorica ad Herennium; Cicero De Oratore; Quintilian) plus any modern empirical work on loci-for-connected-discourse yield CONCRETE, ACTIONABLE encoding guidance for memorizing a coherent TLA+ spec AS A NARRATIVE SEQUENCE?

DELIVER: (1) how orators chunked/sequenced connected discourse via loci (the actual technique, not just that they did it); (2) a translation to spec-as-narrative — how to chunk a ~typical TLA+ specimen's token sequence into loci-able units; (3) any empirical efficacy data on loci for connected/coherent (not list) material; (4) concrete recommendations that feed the C3 learning-protocol spec (the loci/chain encoding method + operator-card design). Peer-reviewed + primary classical sources required.

GROUNDS: C3 (learning-protocol spec) of the design cycle. Findings → capture as a decision/research drawer in tla_puzzles/decisions; close bead; record back into the design-doc C3 marker.
close_reason: C4 research complete; findings filed in drawer_tla_puzzles_decisions_ebd286000153c745c946963e and precipitated into design-cycle decision D7 (learning protocol). Key results: ad-res>ad-verbum, encode-from-audio-not-reading, encode-then-test composition.

title: Audit ~106 puzzles for QG rule-2 violations (smuggled + mis-demoed)
description:
Goal: Produce a comprehensive findings drawer cataloging every QG rule-2 violation across the ~106 fully-implemented puzzles. Read-only research bead — no code changes here.

Files (read-only):
- puzzles/*/README.md (lesson + worked example + puzzle text)
- puzzles/*/solution/*.tla (actual constructs used)
- docs/curriculum/*/T??.md, R??.md, J??.md (per-puzzle pages with builds-on chain)
- bd labels (concept tags per puzzle, if present)
- QUALITY_GATE.md (the rule definitions)

Scope: only fully-implemented puzzles (~106). Skip stubs/scaffolds.

Method (per puzzle):
1. Identify the claimed "one new thing" from the lesson section.
2. Extract every TLA+/PlusCal construct used in the solution.
3. Compute should-already-know set = union of constructs introduced by all puzzles in the transitive `builds-on` chain.
4. Smuggled = (constructs in solution) − (claimed new concept) − (should-already-know set).
5. Mis-demoed check — for each construct the lesson claims to introduce: does the worked example demonstrate it canonically and non-gratuitously? Flag self-contradicting demos (e.g., T04's `goto`s that say "use this to divert flow" but mostly go to the next sequential label).
6. Note when a demo deliberately uses a non-idiomatic form for pedagogical purposes — that's allowed IF the lesson annotates it as such, otherwise it's a violation.

Output: one MemPalace drawer in `tla_puzzles/curriculum`, table-shaped:
| puzzle | claimed concept | smuggled[] | mis-demoed[] | severity (low/med/high) | suggested fix shape (extract upstream / new puzzle / inline-explain / annotate-as-demonstrative) |

Steps:
1. Enumerate fully-implemented puzzles (filter the puzzles/ dir, drop stubs).
2. Walk per puzzle through the method above (consider parallel sub-agents per tier).
3. Cross-check T04 entries against existing diagnosis drawer (drawer_tla_puzzles_curriculum_94e328409a3c5ac27ba69d27) — they should agree.
4. File the findings drawer.
5. Add bd notes on this bead linking to the drawer ID.

Acceptance:
- Every fully-implemented puzzle has a row.
- T04 entries match the prior diagnosis drawer (self = smuggled, goto = mis-demoed).
- Findings drawer ID recorded in bd notes on this bead.
- Findings inform the per-fix beads filed afterward (those beads are NOT created here).
notes: Audit complete 2026-05-06. Findings drawer: drawer_tla_puzzles_curriculum_45aa23d4d99a54513e81d6d0 (tla_puzzles/curriculum). 3 REVISE: T04 (process-set+self bundle, confirmed), T11 (\o + SubSeq bundle, confirmed), T22 (IF-expression + CASE bundle, NEW finding). 7 PASS-borderline. CONTRADICTION SURFACED: T04 goto mis-demo claim from diagnosis drawer is REFUTED — gotos in T04 demo are non-gratuitous per the lesson's own rule. Frank to adjudicate.
close_reason: QG rule 2 audit complete: 3 REVISE (T04, T11, T22) + 5 PASS-borderline. Findings in drawer 45aa23d4d99a54513e81d6d0. Two methodological principles locked. Fix beads (.2/.3/.4) deferred per acceptance criteria.

title: Curriculum QG rule-2 audit + T04 self-smuggling fix
description:
Goal: Eliminate QG rule-2 (Minimal Novelty) violations across the curriculum.

Trigger: T04 (Broken Door) smuggles `self` keyword (docs/curriculum/tier-1/T04.md:66) and `goto` (mis-demoed — 2/3 gratuitous gotos that don't divert flow). Frank flagged 2026-05-06.

Design (locked 2026-05-06):
- Audit all ~106 fully-implemented puzzles for two violation types:
  (A) Smuggled — construct used in solution but never lesson-introduced.
  (B) Mis-demoed — claimed-introduced construct demonstrated non-canonically (e.g., T04's gratuitous gotos refuting their own rule). Includes "unannotated demonstrative form" (lesson uses non-idiomatic constructs for teaching but doesn't say so).
- Audit-first, fix-second ordering. Single epic; audit child blocks fix children.
- Prior locked tier-1 = 8 puzzles is open for revision. Specifically:
  - Insert new T04: Roll Call (lesson worked example) / Group Photo (puzzle setting). Race-free, single-label, exercises `done := done \union {self}`. Teaches process-set `\in` syntax + `self` keyword as one cohesive concept.
  - Current T04 (Broken Door) → T05; cascade T05-T08 → T06-T09. Tier 1 = 9 puzzles.
  - Fix recipe library gains a "demonstrative-form-with-annotation" pattern (e.g., for T04's gotos: keep contrived form for naming, show idiomatic form alongside, annotate the difference).

Fix beads filed AFTER audit, since audit may surface adjacent violations that batch-fix together.

Cross-refs:
- MemPalace drawer: drawer_tla_puzzles_curriculum_94e328409a3c5ac27ba69d27 (diagnosis)
- QUALITY_GATE.md rules 1, 2, 7 (the relevant pedagogy rules)
- docs/curriculum/tier-1/T04.md:66 (smuggled `self`)
- docs/curriculum/tier-2/R03.md (calls itself a "recap" of T04)

Acceptance:
- Audit findings drawer filed in tla_puzzles/curriculum with table: puzzle | claimed concept | smuggled[] | mis-demoed[] | severity | suggested fix shape.
- Each violation has a fix bead under this epic.
- Tier-1 cascade lands cleanly with no stale builds-on links across docs/, site/, R03.md, CURRICULUM_MAP.md.

notes:
2026-05-06 (working tla-0w8.2): cascade decision SUPERSEDED — see drawer_tla_puzzles_decisions_7792629c5a7545457eb02de5 supersession block.

Original plan (description above) had `current T04 → T05; cascade T05-T08 → T06-T09; tier 1 = 9 puzzles`. This collides with existing T09-records (tla-nh4) — puzzle slugs are flat at puzzles/ root, globally unique. Locked design didn't note the collision.

Zero risk to bookmarks/build scripts. Tier 1 still grows 8 → 9 puzzles, but as T01, T02, T03, T03b, T04, T05, T06, T07, T08 (no renames).

- tla-0w8.3 (split T11) and tla-0w8.4 (split T22) — likely also benefit from suffix-style (T11 + T11b for SubSeq; T22 + T22b for CASE) per same precedent. Confirm with Frank when claiming each.

Decisions #1-#5 and #7 of the locked design remain in force. Decision #6 superseded.
close_reason: Superseded by the v2 rebuild (tla-qpm). The epic's premise — enforce QG rule 2 (minimal novelty) more rigorously across the curriculum — is inverted by the post-mortem: 'exactly one new concept' + minimal novelty mechanically produces puzzles that are near-copies of the lesson example, which is the failure v1 died of. v2 organizes around modeling situations with coverage as an end-of-run audit. title: verify-puzzle.sh: copy helper modules to scratch dir
description: Tier 6 audit (tla-3vt.6) surfaced that verify-puzzle.sh copies only <base>.tla + .cfg to its scratch dir, omitting helper modules (e.g., AbstractCard.tla, Counter.tla, OrderStates.tla, Timer.tla, CounterA.tla, RingCount.tla, AbstractLight.tla, AbstractSignal.tla). When TLC tries to resolve a multi-module spec it errors with 'Cannot find source file for module ...', but the elif chain in verify-puzzle.sh falls through to PASS-OTHER (rc=0 because pcal-rc check passes and the script eventually hits 'Finished in'). Net effect: T51, T52, T54-T59 (and likely Tier 5 specs that are multi-module) are NOT actually verified by the gate — they all currently report PASS-OTHER instead of being rejected. Direct TLC runs in each solution/ dir confirm the puzzles themselves are correct. Two possible fixes: (a) copy the entire solution/ dir to scratch (simplest), or (b) detect cross-module FAIL via 'Cannot find source file' / 'Parsing or semantic analysis failed' patterns.
close_reason: copy helper modules to scratch plus harden classifier — multi-module specs T51-T59, R12, C02, T67 now correctly verified via fcb4b15. drawer bcb4fa85 + 7 KG triples + 2 diary entries filed.

title: grade.sh crashes on rc=75/76/77 instead of grading the submission INVALID
description:
`grade.sh`'s `classify` (`:389-405`) routes 150, 151, 255 and 124 to INVALID on the submission
phase, but lets 75, 76 and 77 fall through to `die_harness`.

Those three are learner-facing. `verdict.sh`'s header (bead `tla-i9m`) records them as SPEC_EVAL_
FAILURE, SAFETY_EVAL_FAILURE and LIVENESS_EVAL_FAILURE — "the spec could not be evaluated". A
submission whose observation record has the wrong shape is a learner error, not a harness fault.

Measured: a submission defining `Observe == [hue |-> colour]` against a reference whose obligations
read `o.level` gives `HARNESS ERROR: reference obligation 1: unexpected verdict rc=75`, exit 4.

So the grader crashes instead of grading. Exit 4 is HARNESS_ERROR, which tells a learner nothing
and tells whoever is running the batch that the harness is broken when it is not.

75 is also a family rather than a single cause — four EC constants route to it, recorded during
the `tla-i9m` work — so the INVALID message should say the spec did not evaluate rather than
guessing why.

Found by the `tla-x8s` agent.

close_reason:
Merged as 55c85fa (work commit b71ec34), plus af93ed2 for Gate.tla. Design captured in drawer_tla_puzzles_decisions_89795ff4c47c0358e2ea81e9.

A structureless spec — one variable, any permitted value at any time, no transitions, no causality — passed with zero witnesses against the shipped reference, and its operator was entirely honest, so this was never about lying. Root cause: every obligation was a single-state predicate, and no single-state predicate can constrain a transition relation. References may now state Step_*(o,p) obligations judged as a boxed action subscripted on Observe and declared PROPERTY. The _Observe subscript closes tla-nyrb's atomicity direction by construction. The frozen-operator trapdoor inside that fix is gated by a three-layer landmark check rather than a header note.

Four smaller defects landed with it: REPO_ROOT resolved from the caller's cwd so grading inside another repo ran that repo's verdict channel; rc=75/76/77 crashed the grader instead of grading the submission INVALID; the constants fragment went in unvalidated; and a selftest helper hardcoded one problem's directories. 58 assertions to 86.

Verified on main by central: the structureless spec now returns FAIL, under_constrained true, exit 1, with a real witness location. lint 0, test 0, 10 suites in 191.7s. Fourth site of the fragment-validator class filed separately.

title: §5.6's hand procedure dirties the .cfg it is checking
description:
§5.6 describes the PlusCal gate as "re-run `pcal` after commenting and require the TRANSLATION
block byte-identical". Followed literally, in the directory holding the artifact, that dirties the
`.cfg`: `pcal` prepends `\* Add statements after this line.` to it. Measured during the pilot's
step 7, md5 `a3c92eb6…` before and `0616a66c…` after.

For a frozen artifact that is a write to a file under hash. The pilot's freeze survived only
because the gate was run on copies.

**`harness/comment-gate.sh` already gets this right** — it stages copies, and running it against
the frozen pair leaves `sha256sum -c FREEZE.sha256` clean. So this is a documentation gap, not a
harness bug. The plan describes a procedure more dangerous than the component that implements it,
and a reader who follows the plan by hand corrupts what they are checking.

Fix: §5.6 should say the re-translation runs on a copy, and point at `comment-gate.sh` rather than
describing a hand procedure that nobody should run.

Found running the tla-kl5.11 pilot, step 7, by the comment-pass agent.

title: cd "" succeeds, so the || exit guard on REPO_ROOT does not close the hazard
description:
Six suites open with `REPO_ROOT=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)` and then `cd "$REPO_ROOT"`.
`tla-5r7` added `|| exit 1` to close SC2164, which handles a cd that fails.

It does not handle the case that actually happens. If `git rev-parse` fails, `REPO_ROOT` is the
empty string, and `cd ""` returns 0 without moving. So the guard passes and the suite runs from
whatever directory it was invoked in.

Cheap to close with an emptiness guard on `REPO_ROOT` before the cd. Reported by the `tla-5r7`
